definition_zh: 云的形成；云的形态；成云过程
definition_en: the process in which moist air cools and its vapour turns into a visible cloud, or a cloud mass so formed
core_image: 山谷里升起的水汽在半山腰遇冷，聚成一团看得见的白絮
scene: 清晨山谷中水汽沿坡上升，在半山腰聚成一团白絮。Orographic lift produced a cloud formation along the ridge by mid-morning.
sceneCN: 这里指「水汽受地形抬升、冷却凝结而成云的过程」（第 1 个义项：湿空气上升冷却、水汽变成可见云体的过程）；句意为地形抬升在上午过半时沿山脊生成了一片云。图中可辨识物件：山坡、上升的水汽、白絮状云团、山脊线。

senses.title: The process by which a cloud comes into being
senses.titleCN: 水汽冷却凝结而成云的过程
senses.definition: the process in which rising moist air cools and its water vapour condenses into a visible cloud
senses.definitionCN: 上升的湿空气冷却、其中的水汽凝结成可见云体的过程
senses.example: Orographic lift produced a cloud formation along the ridge by mid-morning.
senses.exampleCN: 地形抬升在上午过半时沿山脊生成了一片云。
senses.why: Cloud is an Old English word for a mass of rock or hill, later transferred to a mass in the sky; formation comes from Latin forma 'shape' plus -atio, so the phrase names both the shaping and the thing shaped.
senses.whyCN: cloud 是古英语中表示「岩块、山丘」的词，后来移指天上的团块；formation 来自拉丁 forma「形状」加 -atio，因此这个短语同时指「成形」与「成形之物」。

senses.title: A visible cloud mass of a particular shape
senses.titleCN: 具有特定形状的可见云体
senses.definition: a body of cloud with a recognisable outline as seen from the ground
senses.definitionCN: 从地面看去轮廓可辨的一团云
senses.example: A striking cloud formation hung over the valley at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 黄昏时一片引人注目的云悬在山谷上方。
senses.why: The noun formation can name the result as well as the act, so a cloud formation is simply a formation made of cloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词 formation 既可指动作也可指结果，因此 cloud formation 就是「由云构成的成形之物」。

senses.title: The condensation step onto tiny nuclei
senses.titleCN: 水汽在凝结核上凝结的环节
senses.definition: the microphysical step in which vapour condenses on dust, salt or ice nuclei
senses.definitionCN: 水汽在尘埃、盐粒或冰核等凝结核上凝结的微观环节
senses.example: Dust from the dry lakebed sped up cloud formation downwind.
senses.exampleCN: 干涸湖床扬起的尘埃加快了下风方向的成云。
senses.why: Formation here narrows to one stage of the process, because droplets need a surface before they can appear.
senses.whyCN: 这里的 formation 收窄为过程中的一个环节，因为液滴必须先有依附的表面才能出现。

senses.title: An organised cloud pattern seen from above
senses.titleCN: 从空中看到的成片云系格局
senses.definition: an organised pattern of cloud tops visible in satellite imagery
senses.definitionCN: 卫星图像中可见的、有组织的云顶分布格局
senses.example: The satellite tracked cloud formation over the basin each hour.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星每小时追踪该盆地上空的成云格局。
senses.why: Seen from orbit the emphasis shifts from one cloud to the arrangement, and formation takes its sense of an ordered pattern.
senses.whyCN: 从轨道上看，重点从一朵云转到云的排列，formation 于是取「有秩序的格局」之义。

senses.title: A recognised cloud type in a classification
senses.titleCN: 云分类体系中的一个云型
senses.definition: one of the named genera or species of cloud used in meteorological classification
senses.definitionCN: 气象分类中命名的云属或云种之一
senses.example: The observer logged the cloud formation as altocumulus lenticularis.
senses.exampleCN: 观测员把这片云记为荚状高积云。
senses.why: Meteorology borrowed the phrase for the units of its classification, since each type is a stable, repeatable shape.
senses.whyCN: 气象学借用这个短语来指分类的单位，因为每一类都是一种稳定、可重复的形状。

senses.title: Cloud created by human action
senses.titleCN: 由人为作用生成的云
senses.definition: cloud produced deliberately by seeding or unintentionally by an industrial plume
senses.definitionCN: 通过播撒作业有意生成、或由工业烟羽无意生成的云
senses.example: Seeding the deck led to cloud formation within twenty minutes.
senses.exampleCN: 对云层播撒后二十分钟内便出现了成云。
senses.why: The phrase needed no new word for artificial clouds; formation simply took an agent, human or otherwise.
senses.whyCN: 人造云不需要新词，formation 只要带上施动者即可，无论这施动者是人还是别的因素。

senses.title: A dense mass of things resembling cloud
senses.titleCN: 比喻：形似云团的密集聚集物
senses.definition: a dense gathering of dust, insects or particles that looks like a cloud
senses.definitionCN: 尘埃、昆虫或微粒密集聚拢、形似云团的状态
senses.example: A cloud formation of midges rose from the marsh at sunset.
senses.exampleCN: 日落时沼泽上方升起一片形似云团的蠓虫。
senses.why: Because cloud had long meant any drifting mass, the phrase extends naturally to anything that hangs and moves like one.
senses.whyCN: cloud 早已泛指任何飘浮的团块，因此这个短语自然延伸到一切像云那样悬浮移动的东西。

senses.title: The stage at which an idea takes shape
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：想法开始成形的阶段
senses.definition: the point at which an idea or plan begins to take a visible, workable shape
senses.definitionCN: 想法或计划开始呈现出可见、可操作的形态的阶段
senses.example: The proposal was still in cloud formation when the budget froze.
senses.exampleCN: 预算冻结时，这个提案还处在刚刚成形的阶段。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the physical steps: something scattered gathers, cools and becomes one visible body.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了物理步骤：散乱之物聚拢、冷却，最后成为一个可见的整体。

intro.en: Cloud formation joins an Old English word for a mass of rock with a Latin-derived noun of shaping. The compound itself is modern and transparent. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cloud formation 由一个古英语的「岩块」词与一个拉丁来源的「成形」名词合成。这个复合词本身是近代的，构词透明。年代均为约数。

items.en: Clud meant 'a mass of rock, a hill'. The sense 'visible mass in the sky' is recorded from the thirteenth century, probably through the image of a heap floating overhead.
items.cn: clūd 意为「岩块、山丘」。指「天上的可见团块」的义项自十三世纪有记录，可能来自「悬浮的堆积物」这一意象。

items.en: Forma meant 'shape, mould, outline'. Its deeper origin is not established; the link sometimes proposed to Greek morphē is a hypothesis rather than a proven cognate.
items.cn: forma 意为「形状、模子、轮廓」。其更深来源未得到证明；有人提出的与希腊 morphē 的联系只是假说，并非已证实的同源关系。

items.en: Formare 'to shape' plus -atio produced formatio 'a shaping, a forming', the direct source of English formation.
items.cn: formare「使成形」加 -atio 构成 formatio「成形、塑造」，是英语 formation 的直接来源。

items.en: Cloud and formation were combined in English scientific writing to name the making of a cloud; the phrase is a native construction, not a Latin loan.
items.cn: cloud 与 formation 在英语科技写作中组合起来，用来指云的形成；这个短语是英语自身的构造，并非拉丁语借词。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the phrase was fixed in meteorology both for the process and for a classified cloud shape.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，这个短语在气象学中固定下来，既指过程，也指分类上的云形。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): the pre-Old-English origin of clud is unsettled and is related to clod; any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction. The first date of the compound is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：clūd 在古英语之前的来源无定论，与 clod 有亲缘；凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构。该复合词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds other cloud compounds that share the element cloud but name different things; group two holds words for cloud, cloudiness and the underlying condensation.
note.cn: 第一组是同样含 cloud 一词、但所指不同的复合词；第二组是表示云、云量以及底层凝结过程的词。

entries.definition: The share of the sky obscured by cloud, a measured quantity rather than a process of forming.
entries.definitionCN: 天空被云遮蔽的比例，是一个可测量的量，而非成云的过程。

entries.definition: The practice of adding particles to a cloud to make it rain; it acts on an existing cloud instead of naming its formation.
entries.definitionCN: 向云中播撒微粒以促降水的作业；它作用于已有的云，而不指云的形成。

entries.definition: A brief, violent downpour; it names the precipitation that follows, not the cloud that produced it.
entries.definitionCN: 短促猛烈的暴雨；它指随之而来的降水，而非造出降水的云。

entries.definition: The visible mass of droplets in the sky; cloud formation names how that mass comes about.
entries.definitionCN: 空中可见的液滴团块；cloud formation 指这团块如何生成。

entries.definition: The condition of being cloudy, a state measured over time, while formation is an event with stages.
entries.definitionCN: 多云的状态，是随时间测量的状态，而成形是有阶段的事件。

entries.definition: The change from vapour to liquid, one step within cloud formation rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 由气态变为液态，是成云过程中的一步，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Cloud was first a heap of rock; a heap in the sky kept the same name.
normal.cn: cloud 最初指一堆岩石；天上的堆状物沿用了同一个名字。

normal.en: Formation is forma 'shape' plus -atio, so the phrase is literally 'cloud shaping'.
normal.cn: formation 是 forma「形状」加 -atio，因此这个短语字面就是「云的成形」。

normal.en: The family runs form, formation, formative, reform, conform and formless.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 form、formation、formative、reform、conform 与 formless。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the process sense: cloud formation process, rapid cloud formation, cloud formation and precipitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出过程义：成云过程、快速成云、成云与降水。

normal.en: Meteorology uses the phrase for a classified shape, as in altocumulus lenticularis.
normal.cn: 气象学用这个短语指分类上的云形，如荚状高积云。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle's steam gathering into one white shape under a cold window.
abstract.cn: 想象水壶的蒸汽在冷窗前聚成一个白色的形状。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd drifting together until it has a visible outline.
abstract.cn: 想象人群慢慢聚拢，直到有了看得见的轮廓。

abstract.en: Picture a rough idea cooling into a shape you could hand to someone.
abstract.cn: 想象一个粗糙的想法冷却定型，成了可以交给别人的东西。

examples.en: The satellite tracked cloud formation over the basin each hour.
examples.cn: 卫星每小时追踪该盆地上空的成云。

examples.en: Warm ocean air drives cloud formation along the coast.
examples.cn: 温暖的海洋空气推动沿岸成云。

examples.en: A striking cloud formation hung over the valley at dusk.
examples.cn: 黄昏时一片引人注目的云悬在山谷上方。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「cloud（云）+ formation（形成）」——水汽在天上排队成形 → 云的形成

root: 英语复合词：cloud 来自古英语 clūd「岩块、山丘」，后移指天上的云团，更深来源不确定；formation 来自拉丁 forma「形状」加 -atio。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one event: scattered vapour gathers, cools, becomes a visible body, is classified, is seen from above, is made on purpose, and finally lends its shape to dust clouds and to ideas.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个事件展开：散乱的水汽聚拢、冷却、成为可见的团块，被分类、被从空中看到、被人为制造，最后把「成形」这一形状借给尘埃团与想法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour rising along a slope cools and gathers into one white mass.
core.cn: 核心意象：水汽沿坡上升、遇冷，聚成一团白絮。

branches.en: MAKING: the process and its microphysical step both describe vapour becoming droplets.
branches.cn: 生成：过程与其中的微观环节都描述水汽变成液滴。

branches.en: SHAPE SEEN: from the ground or from orbit, the point is an outline one can recognise.
branches.cn: 所见之形：无论从地面还是从轨道，要点都是可辨认的轮廓。

branches.en: CLASSIFICATION: a repeatable shape becomes a named type.
branches.cn: 分类：可重复的形状成为一个有名字的类型。

branches.en: MADE ON PURPOSE: seeding works on the same steps with an added agent.
branches.cn: 人为制造：播撒作业在同一批步骤上加入施动者。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED SHAPE: dust clouds and ideas borrow the gathering outline.
branches.cn: 形状转移：尘埃团与想法借用了这种聚拢的轮廓。

intro.en: The phrase is a native English compound whose second element is a Latin derivative, so it can be read both as English words and as morphemes.
intro.cn: 这个短语是英语自身的复合词，第二个成分是拉丁来源的派生词，因此既可以按英语词读，也可以按语素读。

latinIntro.en: Latin forma gives form, formation, formative and formless; the prefix in reform and conform comes from re- 'again' and con- 'together'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 forma 衍生 form、formation、formative 与 formless；reform 与 conform 的前缀分别来自 re-「再」与 con-「共同」。

items.structure: clūd (Old English noun, 'mass of rock, hill')
items.meaning: a heap; later a sky mass
items.example: A cloud hid the ridge by noon.
items.exampleCN: 到正午时一朵云遮住了山脊。

items.example: The mould gave the clay its form.

items.meaning: the act or result of doing
items.example: The formation of ice took one night.
Those years were formative for her.
items.exampleCN: 那些年对她有塑造作用。

items.example: The fog was grey and formless.

items.meaning: to fit into a shape or rule
items.example: The parts conform to the standard.
Cloud-forming air moved in from the sea.
items.exampleCN: 成云的空气从海上移入。

definition_zh: 凝结；冷凝；缩合；浓缩；凝练；摘要
definition_en: the change of a vapour into a liquid, the drops so formed, or the act of making something denser or shorter
core_image: 冷玻璃杯壁上慢慢爬满细小的水珠，杯外的空气一直往杯壁靠拢
scene: 夏天的冰水杯放在桌上，杯壁很快蒙上一层细密水珠。Condensation covered the outside of the glass within a minute.
sceneCN: 这里指「空气中的水汽遇冷变成液态水的过程」（第 1 个义项：气态水转变为液态水的过程）；句意为一分钟之内凝结的水便盖满了玻璃杯外壁。图中可辨识物件：冰水杯、杯壁水珠、桌面水痕、窗上水汽。

pos.zh: 凝结；冷凝；缩合；浓缩；凝练；摘要

senses.title: Vapour turning into liquid
senses.titleCN: 水汽变为液态水的过程
senses.definition: the process in which a gas or vapour changes into a liquid as it cools
senses.definitionCN: 气体或蒸汽遇冷转变为液体的过程
senses.example: Condensation covered the outside of the glass within a minute.
senses.exampleCN: 一分钟之内凝结的水便盖满了玻璃杯外壁。
senses.why: Latin condensare 'to make dense' was applied by physics to vapour packing into liquid, since the same material becomes far denser.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 condensare「使变密」被物理学用于水汽聚成液体，因为同样的物质变得密得多。

senses.title: The drops that form on a cool surface
senses.titleCN: 冷表面上凝出的水珠
senses.definition: the small drops of liquid left on a cooler surface when vapour condenses
senses.definitionCN: 水汽凝结时在较冷表面上留下的小液滴
senses.example: He wiped the condensation from the bathroom mirror.
senses.exampleCN: 他擦掉了浴室镜面上的水珠。
senses.why: The result and the process share one noun, so the drops themselves are called condensation.
senses.whyCN: 结果与过程共用同一个名词，因此水珠本身也被称作 condensation。

senses.title: A chemical reaction joining two molecules
senses.titleCN: 化学中的缩合反应
senses.definition: a reaction in which two molecules join and a small molecule such as water is released
senses.definitionCN: 两个分子结合并释放出一个小分子（如水）的反应
senses.example: The ester condensation released a molecule of water.
senses.exampleCN: 这步酯缩合释放出一分子水。
senses.why: Two molecules become one dense product while a fragment leaves, which chemists described with the same word as vapour packing together.
senses.whyCN: 两个分子合成一个紧密产物、同时留下一个小碎片，化学家便用与「水汽聚密」相同的词来描述。

senses.title: Deliberate liquefaction of a vapour
senses.titleCN: 有意把蒸汽液化的冷凝操作
senses.definition: the industrial or laboratory act of cooling a vapour so that it becomes liquid
senses.definitionCN: 工业或实验中通过降温使蒸汽变成液体的操作
senses.example: Condensation of the distillate began as soon as the coil cooled.
senses.exampleCN: 盘管一冷却，馏出物的冷凝就开始了。
senses.why: Technology turned the natural process into a controlled step, and kept the noun for the operation.
senses.whyCN: 技术把自然过程变成可控的工序，并沿用同一个名词指这项操作。

senses.title: Making a liquid more concentrated
senses.titleCN: 使液体变浓的浓缩
senses.definition: the act of removing water or solvent so that a liquid becomes stronger
senses.definitionCN: 除去水或溶剂，使液体变得更浓的操作
senses.example: Slow condensation of the broth deepened its flavour.
senses.exampleCN: 汤汁慢慢浓缩，味道更浓了。
senses.why: Making a substance dense is the literal core of condensare, and removing water is the everyday way to do it.
senses.whyCN: 使物质变密是 condensare 的字面核心，而除去水分就是日常做法。

senses.title: Compressing writing or thought
senses.titleCN: 把文字或思想压缩凝练
senses.definition: the act of shortening a text or an argument while keeping its essential content
senses.definitionCN: 在保留核心内容的前提下压缩文字或论证
senses.example: The editing was an exercise in condensation, not deletion.
senses.exampleCN: 这次编辑是压缩凝练，而不是删削。
senses.why: Dense speech was pictured as vapour packed into drops, so shortening a text without losing meaning took the same name.
senses.whyCN: 浓缩的言语被比作水汽聚成液滴，因此在不丢内容的前提下缩短文本也用了同一个词。

senses.title: A shortened version of a text
senses.titleCN: 凝练后的简本、摘要
senses.definition: a shortened form of a longer work, produced by condensing it
senses.definitionCN: 由长文压缩而成的简略版本
senses.example: The journal printed a condensation of the report.
senses.exampleCN: 期刊刊登了这份报告的简本。
senses.why: The product of condensing inherited the noun, so a condensation can be a thing you read.
senses.whyCN: 压缩的产物继承了同一个名词，因此 condensation 也可以指一篇可读的简本。

senses.title: Pressing powder into a dense solid
senses.titleCN: 把粉末压成致密固体
senses.definition: the densification of a powder or material by pressure or heat
senses.definitionCN: 通过压力或加热使粉末或材料致密化的过程
senses.example: Condensation of the powder gave a hard ceramic disc.
senses.exampleCN: 粉末经压制致密化，得到坚硬的陶瓷圆片。
senses.why: Materials science returned to the literal sense: particles brought close together until the mass is dense.
senses.whyCN: 材料学回到字面义：颗粒被压到一起，直到整体变得致密。

senses.title: A quantum state of shared particles
senses.titleCN: 物理学中的凝聚态
senses.definition: the process by which many particles fall into a single low-energy quantum state
senses.definitionCN: 大量粒子进入同一个低能量子态的过程
senses.example: The lab reached condensation at a fraction of a degree above absolute zero.
senses.exampleCN: 该实验室在略高于绝对零度处实现了凝聚。
senses.why: Physics extended density of number to density of state: many particles occupying one state, hence the same word.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把「数量之密」延伸为「状态之密」：大量粒子占据同一状态，因此沿用这个词。

intro.en: Condensation comes from Latin condensare 'to make dense', built on com- 'together' and densare 'to thicken' from densus 'dense'. The physics sense is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: condensation 来自拉丁 condensare「使变密」，由 com-「一起」与 densare「使变厚」构成，后者出自 densus「密的」。物理义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Densus meant 'thick, dense, crowded'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the connection sometimes drawn to a root meaning 'to flow' is conjectural.
items.cn: densus 意为「浓的、密的、拥挤的」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与一个意为「流」的词根相联系，那只是推测。

items.en: Densare 'to make thick' added the causative suffix -are to densus, giving a verb for crowding things together.
items.cn: densare「使变厚」由 densus 加使役后缀 -are 构成，表示把东西挤到一起。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus densare produced condensare 'to press together, make dense', used of air, liquids and writing alike.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 densare 构成 condensare「压紧、使密」，空气、液体与文字都可用它。

items.en: The verb entered English in the sixteenth century; the noun condensation followed, first for thickening and later for the change of state.
items.cn: 动词在十六世纪进入英语，名词 condensation 随后出现，先指变浓，后指物态变化。

items.en: From the nineteenth century chemistry named joining reactions and physics named vapour-to-liquid change with this word, both cases of parts packing closer.
items.cn: 从十九世纪起，化学用它命名结合反应，物理学用它命名气液转变，两者都是成分挤得更近。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): densus has no established ancestor, so every Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction. The first date of the noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：densus 没有已确定的祖先，凡为其提出的印欧形式均属重构。名词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike nouns built on the same root with different endings; group two holds neighbours in the water cycle or in shortening.
note.cn: 第一组是同出一词根、词尾不同的形近名词；第二组是水循环或压缩缩短方面的近义词。

entries.definition: The liquid or solid left after condensation, a material rather than a process.
entries.definitionCN: 凝结之后留下的液体或固体，是物质而非过程。

entries.definition: A device built to condense vapour; the machine, not the change it produces.
entries.definitionCN: 用来冷凝蒸汽的装置；指机器而非它所引起的变化。

entries.definition: Reduction of volume by pressure, often without any change of state; condensation changes state, not always volume.
entries.definitionCN: 靠压力减小体积，通常不涉及物态变化；凝结改变的是物态。

entries.definition: The pressing of solid particles into a denser mass, close to the materials sense of condensation but with no vapour involved.
entries.definitionCN: 把固体颗粒压成更密的块体，接近 condensation 的材料义，但不涉及蒸汽。

entries.definition: Water falling from clouds as rain, snow or hail; condensation comes before it in the water cycle.
entries.definitionCN: 水以雨、雪或雹的形式从云中落下；在水循环中凝结先于它。

entries.definition: The change from liquid to vapour, the reverse of condensation.
entries.definitionCN: 由液态变为气态，是凝结的逆过程。

entries.definition: Shortening by cutting letters or syllables, a mechanical trim rather than the packed rewriting condensation implies.
entries.definitionCN: 靠删字母或音节来缩短，是机械删减，而非 condensation 所含的压缩改写。

entries.definition: A brief statement of the main points; a condensation of a text is one way to produce a summary.
entries.definitionCN: 对要点的简短陈述；文本的缩本正是产生摘要的一种方式。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + densare 'make dense': the parts are packed together.
normal.cn: con-「一起」+ densare「使密」：把成分压到一起。

normal.en: The relative set is condense, condenser, condensate, condensable and condensed.
normal.cn: 同族词有 condense、condenser、condensate、condensable 与 condensed。

normal.en: Water changes state: evaporation up, condensation down. The two nouns are opposites.
normal.cn: 水的物态变化：上升是蒸发，下降是凝结，两个名词正好相反。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the science: condensation reaction, condensation point, condensation trail.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出科学义：缩合反应、凝点、凝结尾迹。

normal.en: The everyday sign is drops on a cold glass or on a bathroom mirror.
normal.cn: 日常标志是冷玻璃杯或浴室镜面上的水珠。

abstract.en: Picture a long letter folded smaller and smaller until only its core is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一封长信被折得越来越小，最后只剩核心。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a corridor pressed shoulder to shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象走廊里的人被挤得肩挨着肩。

abstract.en: Picture mist touching a cold pane and turning into beads you can wipe.
abstract.cn: 想象雾气碰到冷玻璃，变成可以擦掉的珠子。

examples.en: Condensation on the inner pane froze overnight into fern-like patterns.
examples.cn: 内层窗玻璃上的凝结水一夜之间冻成了蕨叶状花纹。

examples.en: The reaction is a condensation that gives off one molecule of water.
examples.cn: 这个反应是脱去一分子水的缩合。

examples.en: Readers preferred the condensation to the full three-volume report.
examples.cn: 读者更喜欢那份三卷报告的简本。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（共同）+ dense（密）」——水汽挤到一起变密，就成了水珠 → 凝结

root: 拉丁 condensare「压紧、使密」= com-（一起）+ densare（使变厚）← densus「密的」；densus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one gesture: parts are pressed closer. Vapour becomes drops, drops coat a glass, molecules join, liquids thicken, texts shorten, and finally many particles share one quantum state.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个动作展开：把成分压得更近。水汽变成水珠，水珠铺在杯壁上，分子彼此结合，液体变浓，文字变短，最后大量粒子共处一个量子态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: vapour crowding onto a cold surface until it becomes visible liquid.
core.cn: 核心意象：水汽挤到冷表面上，直到变成看得见的液体。

branches.en: CHANGE OF STATE: natural cooling and controlled liquefaction are the same transition.
branches.cn: 物态变化：自然冷却与受控液化是同一种转变。

branches.en: DENSER RESULT: drops on a pane and a thickened broth both show material packed closer.
branches.cn: 更密的结果：窗上的水珠与变浓的汤汁都显示物质挤得更紧。

branches.en: MOLECULES JOIN: chemistry applies packing to bonds, with a small fragment leaving.
branches.cn: 分子结合：化学把「挤紧」用于化学键，同时放出小碎片。

branches.en: TEXT PACKED: meaning is kept while the wording is squeezed, and the squeezed product is readable.
branches.cn: 文字压缩：词句被挤压而意义保留，压出的成品可以阅读。

branches.en: MATTER AND STATE PRESSED: powder densifies, and particles crowd into one state.
branches.cn: 物质与状态被压紧：粉末致密化，粒子挤进同一状态。

intro.en: Condensation is a Latin verbal noun whose prefix, root and suffix all recur in English technical vocabulary.
intro.cn: condensation 是拉丁动词性名词，其前缀、词根与后缀在英语科技词汇中反复出现。

latinIntro.en: Latin densus 'dense' gives dense, density and densify; com- 'together' also appears in combine and compress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 densus「密的」衍生 dense、density 与 densify；com-「一起」也出现在 combine 与 compress 中。

items.example: The prefix says the parts are brought together.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀表示成分被聚到一起。

items.example: A dense fog closed the road.

items.exampleCN: 这份笔记把论证压缩了。

latinEntries.structure: densus, densa, densum (adjective, first and second declension)

definition_zh: 使凝结；使浓缩；压缩；精简；使聚集
definition_en: to make a vapour turn to liquid, to make something thicker or shorter, or to bring parts closer together
core_image: 一只手把一团松散的文字往中间按，纸面越按越紧，字还在
scene: 厨房里锅盖边缘不断冒出白汽，厨师把火调小，白汽就在锅盖上凝成水珠流回锅里。Steam will condense on the lid and run back into the pot.
sceneCN: 这里指「蒸汽遇冷变成液态水」（第 1 个义项：使气体或蒸汽转变为液体）；句意为蒸汽在锅盖上凝结成水珠，又流回锅里。图中可辨识物件：汤锅、锅盖、白汽、下流的水珠。

pos.zh: 使凝结；使浓缩；压缩；精简

collocations.phrase: condense the report into one page

senses.title: Make a vapour become liquid
senses.titleCN: 使蒸汽冷凝成液体
senses.definition: to cause a gas or vapour to change into a liquid by cooling or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 通过降温或加压使气体或蒸汽变成液体
senses.example: Steam condensed on the lid and ran back into the pot.
senses.exampleCN: 蒸汽在锅盖上凝结成水珠，又流回锅里。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind condensation: condensare meant 'to press together', and cooling a vapour presses its molecules into liquid form.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 condensation 背后的动作：condensare 意为「压紧」，而冷却蒸汽就是把分子压成液态。

senses.title: Form drops on a cool surface
senses.titleCN: 在冷表面上凝出水珠
senses.definition: to appear as drops of liquid on a surface cooler than the surrounding air
senses.definitionCN: 在比周围空气更冷的表面上以液滴形式出现
senses.example: Moist air condenses on the outside of a cold bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 湿空气在冷瓶子的外壁上凝成水珠。
senses.why: The same physical step seen from the surface's point of view: what lands there is condensed vapour.
senses.whyCN: 这是同一个物理步骤从表面的角度看：落到表面上的是凝下来的水汽。

senses.title: Make a liquid thicker
senses.titleCN: 使液体变浓、变稠
senses.definition: to reduce a liquid by evaporation so that it becomes thicker or stronger
senses.definitionCN: 通过蒸发减少液体，使其变得更稠或更浓
senses.example: Simmer the stock until it condenses to half its volume.
senses.exampleCN: 把高汤慢炖到体积浓缩一半。
senses.why: Removing water packs the remaining solids closer, which is the literal sense of making dense.
senses.whyCN: 去掉水分使剩下的固体挤得更近，这正是「使密」的字面义。

senses.title: Compress a gas into a smaller volume
senses.titleCN: 把气体压缩到更小的体积
senses.definition: to reduce a gas to a smaller volume, often until it liquefies
senses.definitionCN: 把气体压缩到更小的体积，常常直到液化
senses.example: The pump condenses the gas into a steel cylinder.
senses.exampleCN: 泵把气体压进钢瓶。
senses.why: Pressure and cold do the same work on molecules, so the verb covers both routes to a denser state.
senses.whyCN: 加压与降温对分子做的是同一件事，因此这个动词涵盖通往更密状态的两种途径。

senses.title: Shorten a piece of writing
senses.titleCN: 缩短一篇文章
senses.definition: to make a text shorter by removing what is not essential
senses.definitionCN: 删去非必要部分，使文本变短
senses.example: She condensed the chapter into two tight paragraphs.
senses.exampleCN: 她把这一章压缩成两段紧凑的文字。
senses.why: The metaphor of packing is applied to words: less space, same substance.
senses.whyCN: 「压紧」的比喻被用于文字：占更少的篇幅，装同样的内容。

senses.title: Express much in few words
senses.titleCN: 用很少的话表达很多
senses.definition: to express a large amount of meaning in a compact form
senses.definitionCN: 用紧凑的形式表达大量含义
senses.example: Her style condenses a whole history into one image.
senses.exampleCN: 她的风格把整段历史凝缩进一个意象。
senses.why: This sense stresses meaning rather than length: density of content, not merely fewer pages.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项强调意义而非篇幅：是内容的密度，而不只是页数更少。

senses.title: Gather scattered things into one
senses.titleCN: 把分散之物聚成一个整体
senses.definition: to bring scattered material, light or people into a smaller, denser whole
senses.definitionCN: 把分散的物质、光线或人聚成更小更密的整体
senses.example: The lens condensed the sunlight into a single bright point.
senses.exampleCN: 透镜把阳光聚成一个明亮的光点。
senses.why: The physical core returns: separate rays or particles are brought to one place.
senses.whyCN: 物理核心回归：分散的光线或粒子被聚到一处。

senses.title: Join two molecules with loss of a fragment
senses.titleCN: 化学中脱去小分子的缩合
senses.definition: to combine two molecules chemically while releasing a small molecule
senses.definitionCN: 使两个分子在化学上结合，同时释放出一个小分子
senses.example: The two acids condense to form an ester and water.
senses.exampleCN: 这两种酸缩合生成酯和水。
senses.why: Chemistry borrowed the verb for molecules that join closely and squeeze out a small by-product.
senses.whyCN: 化学借用这个动词，指分子紧密结合并挤出一个小的副产物。

senses.title: Bring a jumble into a compact whole
senses.titleCN: 抽象义：把纷杂之事收拢成紧凑整体
senses.definition: to turn a scattered body of experience or material into a compact, ordered whole
senses.definitionCN: 把散乱的经验或材料收拢成紧凑有序的整体
senses.example: The exhibition condenses a decade of work into one room.
senses.exampleCN: 这场展览把十年的作品收进一个展厅。
senses.why: The abstract sense keeps the gesture of gathering and tightening, with no physical vapour left.
senses.whyCN: 抽象义保留了聚拢与收紧的动作，只是不再有物理上的蒸汽。

intro.en: Condense comes from Latin condensare 'to make dense', through French. The prefix com- means 'together' and densare 'to thicken' comes from densus 'dense'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: condense 经法语来自拉丁 condensare「使变密」。前缀 com- 意为「一起」，densare「使变厚」出自 densus「密的」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Densus 'thick, dense, crowded' described crowds, woods and air. Its deeper origin is unsettled and the forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: densus「浓的、密的、拥挤的」可形容人群、树林与空气。其更深来源无定论，为其提出的形式均属重构。

items.en: The causative verb densare 'to make thick' was formed on densus with -are, so the verb already carried the idea of making something denser.
items.cn: 使役动词 densare「使变厚」由 densus 加 -are 构成，因此这个动词本身已含「使某物更密」的意思。

items.en: Com- 'together' plus densare gave condensare 'to press together, compress, make dense', used of air and of speech.
items.cn: com-「一起」加 densare 构成 condensare「压紧、压缩、使密」，既用于空气，也用于言语。

items.en: Old French condenser carried the verb into English in the sixteenth century, at first for thickening liquids and for shortening speech.
items.cn: 古法语 condenser 在十六世纪把这个动词带入英语，最初用于使液体变稠与缩短言辞。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the verb was used for vapour turning to liquid, and later for chemical joining reactions.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，这个动词用于水汽变为液体，后来又用于化学结合反应。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): densus has no proven ancestor, and any Indo-European root cited for it is a reconstruction. The first English date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：densus 没有已证实的祖先，为其引用的任何印欧词根均属重构。英语首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds verbs built on the same -dense stock or easily mistaken for it; group two holds verbs of shortening and thickening.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 -dense 词干或易与之混淆的动词；第二组是表示缩短与变稠的动词。

entries.definition: Built on premere 'to press', so it reduces volume by pressure and says nothing about changing state.
entries.definitionCN: 由 premere「压」构成，靠压力减小体积，不涉及物态变化。

entries.definition: To press solid material into a denser mass, usually without heat or vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 把固体材料压成更密的块体，通常不涉及热或蒸汽。

entries.definition: From con- plus centrum 'centre': to bring things toward one centre, which is why it names focus as well as strength.
entries.definitionCN: 由 con- 加 centrum「中心」构成：把东西向一个中心聚拢，因此既指聚焦也指变浓。

entries.definition: From de- plus scandere 'to climb': to stoop to a lower level, sharing the con- prefix only by accident of spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 de- 加 scandere「攀登」：屈尊俯就，只是拼写上前缀相同，词源无关。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for making anything shorter; condense adds the idea of keeping content intact.
entries.definitionCN: 使任何东西变短的日常动词；condense 多了「内容保持完整」的意思。

entries.definition: To cut a text down while keeping its structure, closer to trimming than to packing.
entries.definitionCN: 在保留结构的前提删减文本，更接近修剪而非压紧。

entries.definition: To make a liquid or mixture thick, by any means; condense specifies removal of water or vapour.
entries.definitionCN: 用任何方式使液体或混合物变稠；condense 明确指除去水或蒸汽。

entries.definition: To state the main points in brief; it reports content rather than physically shortening the text.
entries.definitionCN: 简要陈述要点；它是转述内容，而非在物理上缩短文本。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: con- 'together' + densare 'make dense': pack it together.
normal.cn: con-「一起」+ densare「使密」：把它压到一起。

normal.en: condense, condensation, condenser, condensate all share the same stem.
normal.cn: condense、condensation、condenser、condensate 同用一个词干。

normal.en: Two directions at once: cool a vapour down, or boil a liquid down.
normal.cn: 两个方向同时成立：把蒸汽冷下来，或把液体煮浓。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: condensed milk, condense a text, condense into droplets.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：炼乳、压缩文本、凝结成液滴。

normal.en: The adjective condensed marks both milk and print, showing the two senses in one form.
normal.cn: 形容词 condensed 既能修饰牛奶也能修饰文字，一个形式显出两个义项。

abstract.en: Picture a sponge squeezed until the water runs out and only the body remains.
abstract.cn: 想象海绵被挤干，水流出，只剩本体。

abstract.en: Picture a long speech folded like a map until one sentence shows the route.
abstract.cn: 想象一段长话像地图那样被折叠，最后一句就显出路线。

abstract.en: Picture many lamps aimed at one point until the light is too bright to look at.
abstract.cn: 想象许多灯对准一点，光聚得让人不敢直视。

examples.en: Cooling coils condense the vapour before it reaches the pump.
examples.cn: 冷却盘管在蒸汽到达泵之前把它冷凝。

examples.en: He can condense a three-hour lecture into ten clear sentences.
examples.cn: 他能把三小时的讲座压缩成十句清楚的话。

examples.en: The acid and the alcohol condense to give an ester and water.
examples.cn: 酸与醇缩合生成酯和水。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「con（一起）+ dense（密）」——把东西压到一起变密 → 凝结、压缩

root: 拉丁 condensare「压紧、使密」= com-（一起）+ densare（使变厚）← densus「密的」；densus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one squeeze: vapour is cooled into liquid, liquid is boiled down, gas is compressed, words are packed, and at last scattered experience is gathered into one compact room.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个「挤压」展开：蒸汽被冷成液体，液体被熬浓，气体被压缩，文字被压紧，最后散乱的经验被收进一个紧凑的空间。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing a loose mass inward until it holds together.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把松散之物往中间按，直到它聚成一体。

branches.en: TURN TO LIQUID: whether in a pot or on a bottle, vapour becomes drops.
branches.cn: 变成液体：无论在锅里还是瓶上，水汽都变成水珠。

branches.en: DENSER MATTER: boiling down and compressing both remove space between particles.
branches.cn: 更密的物质：熬浓与压缩都减少粒子间的空间。

branches.en: FEWER WORDS: length shrinks while meaning stays packed.
branches.cn: 更少的词：篇幅缩短而意义仍被压在其中。

branches.en: ONE POINT: scattered rays or people are brought to a single place.
branches.cn: 一个点：分散的光线或人被聚到同一处。

branches.en: JOINED WHOLE: molecules join, and experience is gathered into one ordered body.
branches.cn: 合成的整体：分子彼此结合，经验被收成一个有序整体。

intro.en: Condense is a Latin verb in which prefix, root and suffix are each productive in English.
intro.cn: condense 是拉丁动词，其前缀、词根与后缀在英语中各自都有构词能力。

latinIntro.en: Latin densus yields dense, density, densify; com- 'together' recurs in compress, combine and collect.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 densus 衍生 dense、density、densify；com-「一起」在 compress、combine、collect 中反复出现。

items.example: A dense crowd filled the square.
The cold turned the mist into drops.
They compressed the gas into a cylinder.
Cool the vapour to condense it.
The book is dense with detail.
Rollers densify the new road base.

definition_zh: 水汽；水蒸气；大气中的气态水
definition_en: water in its gaseous state, especially when present in the air
core_image: 看不见的水以气的形态混在空气里，遇冷才现形为一层水珠
scene: 雨后的柏油路在太阳下冒起若有若无的白气，气象站记录到空气里的水汽在增多。Sunlight raised the water vapor above the wet road until the gauge climbed.
sceneCN: 这里指「混在空气中的气态水」（第 1 个义项：以气体形态存在的水）；句意为阳光使湿路面上方的水汽增多，直到仪表读数上升。图中可辨识物件：湿柏油路、升起的白气、气象仪表、远处云层。

senses.title: Water in the gaseous state
senses.titleCN: 以气态存在的水
senses.definition: water that has turned into gas and is no longer a liquid or a solid
senses.definitionCN: 已变成气体、不再是液体或固体的水
senses.example: Sunlight raised the water vapor above the wet road until the gauge climbed.
senses.exampleCN: 阳光使湿路面上方的水汽增多，直到仪表读数上升。
senses.why: Water is the Old English word for the liquid; vapor is Latin for 'steam'. The compound names the same substance in its gas state.
senses.whyCN: water 是古英语中指这种液体的词，vapor 是拉丁语「蒸汽」，复合词指同一物质的气态。

senses.title: The amount of vapour in the air
senses.titleCN: 空气中水汽的含量
senses.definition: the quantity of gaseous water held in a body of air, measured as humidity
senses.definitionCN: 一定体积空气中含有的气态水量，以湿度计量
senses.example: The sonde reported water vapor rising with height.
senses.exampleCN: 探空仪记录到水汽随高度增加。
senses.why: Meteorology treats the gas as a measurable constituent of air, so the phrase often means an amount rather than a substance.
senses.whyCN: 气象学把这种气体当作空气的可测成分，因此这个短语常指数量而非物质本身。

senses.title: Vapour supplied by evaporation and transpiration
senses.titleCN: 蒸发与蒸腾送出的水汽
senses.definition: gaseous water entering the air from evaporating surfaces and from plants
senses.definitionCN: 从蒸发面与植物进入空气的气态水
senses.example: Forests add water vapor to the air through transpiration.
senses.exampleCN: 森林通过蒸腾向空气补充水汽。
senses.why: The phrase shifts from what the gas is to where it comes from, a flux rather than a stock.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语从「气体是什么」转到「它从哪里来」，指通量而非存量。

senses.title: The raw material of cloud and rain
senses.titleCN: 成云致雨的水汽来源
senses.definition: the vapour that cools and condenses to build clouds and eventually precipitation
senses.definitionCN: 冷却凝结后形成云并最终形成降水的水汽
senses.example: Rising air carries water vapor that later falls as rain.
senses.exampleCN: 上升的空气带着水汽，这些水汽后来以雨的形式落下。
senses.why: Since clouds are made of condensed vapour, the phrase naturally names the supply from which weather is built.
senses.whyCN: 云由凝结的水汽构成，因此这个短语自然指造出天气的那份原料。

senses.title: The strongest greenhouse gas by amount
senses.titleCN: 含量最多的温室气体
senses.definition: gaseous water considered as a gas that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation
senses.definitionCN: 从吸收并再辐射红外辐射的角度看待的气态水
senses.example: Water vapor amplifies every warming that carbon dioxide begins.
senses.exampleCN: 水汽会放大二氧化碳引发的每一分变暖。
senses.why: Climatology counts the gas among greenhouse gases, where its role is stated in the vocabulary of radiation.
senses.whyCN: 气候学把这种气体算作温室气体，此时它的作用用辐射的语言来表述。

senses.title: Steam in engines and boilers
senses.titleCN: 锅炉与热机中的水蒸气
senses.definition: gaseous water used as a working fluid in engines, turbines and heating systems
senses.definitionCN: 在发动机、汽轮机与供暖系统中作为工作介质的气态水
senses.example: The turbine is driven by high-pressure water vapor.
senses.exampleCN: 汽轮机由高压水蒸气驱动。
senses.why: Engineering prefers the same phrase for the working fluid, even when the gas is hot and pressurised rather than atmospheric.
senses.whyCN: 工程上即使气体高温高压、并非大气中的水汽，也沿用同一短语指这种工作介质。

senses.title: Vapour left in an aircraft's trail
senses.titleCN: 飞机凝结尾迹中的水汽
senses.definition: the gaseous water in engine exhaust that condenses into a visible contrail
senses.definitionCN: 发动机尾气中凝结成可见尾迹的气态水
senses.example: Exhaust water vapor froze into a long white trail.
senses.exampleCN: 尾气中的水汽冻成一道长长的白迹。
senses.why: The phrase names the component of exhaust responsible for the trail, tying an observed line in the sky to one gas.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语指尾气中造成尾迹的那个成分，把天上看到的一条线归到一种气体上。

senses.title: Something unseen that carries hidden force
senses.titleCN: 比喻：无形却蓄着力量之物
senses.definition: something invisible that is nevertheless present everywhere and ready to become visible or active
senses.definitionCN: 看不见却无处不在、随时会显形或起作用的东西
senses.example: Rumour spread through the office like water vapor through dry air.
senses.exampleCN: 传闻像水汽渗进干燥空气那样在办公室里扩散。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps two features of the gas: it is invisible, and it becomes visible the moment conditions change.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了这种气体的两个特征：看不见，而条件一变就显形。

intro.en: Water vapor joins the Old English word for water with Latin vapor 'steam'. The compound is transparent and modern, while each part has its own history. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: water vapor 把古英语的「水」与拉丁 vapor「蒸汽」组合起来。复合词透明而属近代，两个成分各有自己的历史。年代均为约数。

items.en: Wæter is the inherited Germanic word for water, matched by forms in other Germanic languages; its Indo-European background is well attested.
items.cn: wæter 是日耳曼语中固有的「水」一词，与其他日耳曼语言的形式对应；其印欧背景有充分证据。

items.en: Vapor meant 'steam, exhalation, warmth'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; no convincing link to a Greek or Indo-European source has been established.
items.cn: vapor 意为「蒸汽、呼出的气、热」。其更深来源不确定，尚未确立与希腊语或印欧语来源的可靠联系。

items.en: Old French vapour carried the word into English, where vapor and vapour competed before vapour became the British spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 vapour 把这个词带入英语，vapor 与 vapour 曾经并存，后来 vapour 成为英式拼法。

items.en: From the eighteenth century water vapor was the standard term for gaseous water in the air, a measurable part of the atmosphere.
items.cn: 从十八世纪起，water vapor 成为空气中气态水的标准说法，是大气中可测量的一部分。

items.en: Twentieth-century climatology added the radiative sense, naming the gas by its absorption of infrared radiation.
items.cn: 二十世纪的气候学加入了辐射义，按其对红外辐射的吸收来界定这种气体。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin only): vapor has no established pre-Latin source, so any root offered for it is a reconstruction. The compound's first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅更深词源）：vapor 没有已确定的拉丁语之前来源，凡为其提出的词根均属重构。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds the spelling variants and compounds that look almost identical; group two holds the related states and names of water.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写几乎相同的变体与复合词；第二组是水在相关状态与名称上的近义词。

entries.definition: The same term spelled with ou, standard in British English; the meaning is identical.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词采用 ou 的英式拼法，意义完全相同。

entries.definition: A rare plural used for several volumes or kinds of vapour; the mass noun is normal in science.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用复数，指多份或多种水汽；科学写作中通常作不可数名词。

entries.definition: The partial pressure exerted by vapour in the air, a measured quantity named from the phrase.
entries.definitionCN: 空气中水汽所产生的分压，是由该短语派生的可测量。

entries.definition: The movement of vapour through the atmosphere, a flux rather than the gas itself.
entries.definitionCN: 水汽在大气中的移动，是通量而非气体本身。

entries.definition: Vapour from boiling water, often visible as a white mist; water vapor can be cold and invisible.
entries.definitionCN: 沸水产生的蒸汽，常呈白雾；water vapor 可以是冷的、看不见的。

entries.definition: Small amounts of water held in air, soil or a substance, not necessarily in gas form.
entries.definitionCN: 空气、土壤或物质中含着少量水，未必是气态。

entries.definition: The amount of vapour in the air as a measured quantity; water vapor is the substance measured.
entries.definitionCN: 空气中水汽的量，是测量值；water vapor 是被测的物质。

entries.definition: Tiny liquid droplets suspended in air; unlike vapour, mist is already liquid.
entries.definitionCN: 悬在空中的微小液滴；与蒸气不同，雾已经是液态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two plain words: water plus vapor 'steam', so the phrase says what the steam is made of.
normal.cn: 两个朴素的词：water 加 vapor「蒸汽」，短语直接说明这蒸汽由什么构成。

normal.en: The relatives run vapor, vaporize, vaporization, vaporous and evaporation.
normal.cn: 同族词有 vapor、vaporize、vaporization、vaporous 与 evaporation。

normal.en: Science measures it as humidity, water vapor pressure or water vapor content.
normal.cn: 科学上用湿度、水汽压或水汽含量来测量它。

normal.en: It is invisible until it condenses, which is why the kettle's spout shows nothing until the air cools.
normal.cn: 它在凝结之前看不见，因此壶嘴在空气变冷前什么也看不出。

normal.en: British writing spells the second word vapour; American writing spells it vapor.
normal.cn: 英式写作把第二个词拼作 vapour，美式写作拼作 vapor。

abstract.en: Picture a room full of something you cannot see but can feel on a cold pane.
abstract.cn: 想象一屋子看不见的东西，却在冷玻璃上摸得到。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd holding its breath, invisible until someone speaks.
abstract.cn: 想象一群人憋着气，在有人开口前看不见。

abstract.en: Picture a whole lake lifted into the sky and waiting to fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一整片湖被抬到天上，等着落下来。

examples.en: Warm air can hold more water vapor than cold air.
examples.cn: 暖空气能容纳的水汽比冷空气多。

examples.en: Satellites map water vapor across the whole Pacific.
examples.cn: 卫星绘制整个太平洋上空的水汽分布。

examples.en: The plume's water vapor condensed into a trail behind the jet.
examples.cn: 尾气中的水汽在喷气机后凝成一条尾迹。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「water（水）+ vapor（蒸汽）」——水变成气，看不见地飘在空中 → 水汽

root: 英语复合词：water 来自古英语 wæter，日耳曼语固有词；vapor 来自拉丁 vapor「蒸汽、呼气」，更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one invisible substance: it is gaseous water, it is measured in air, it rises from surfaces and plants, it builds clouds, it traps heat, it drives turbines, it draws a line behind a jet, and finally it stands for anything unseen that is ready to appear.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种看不见的物质展开：它是气态的水，在空气中被计量，从地表与植物升起，造出云，截住热量，驱动汽轮机，在飞机后画出一条线，最后代表一切看不见却随时显形之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: invisible gas mixed into air, showing itself only when it touches something cold.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的气体混在空气里，只在碰到冷物时才现身。

branches.en: THE SUBSTANCE: in the air or in a boiler, it is water in gas form.
branches.cn: 物质本身：无论在空气中还是在锅炉里，都是气态的水。

branches.en: MEASURED AND MOVED: humidity counts it, and transpiration supplies it.
branches.cn: 被计量与被输送：湿度计它的量，蒸腾供给它。

branches.en: WEATHER MATERIAL: clouds and rain are built from it.
branches.cn: 天气原料：云与雨由它构成。

branches.en: HEAT AND EXHAUST: it absorbs infrared, and it whitens a contrail.
branches.cn: 热量与尾气：它吸收红外，也把尾迹染白。

branches.en: UNSEEN FORCE: what cannot be seen may still fill the room.
branches.cn: 无形之力：看不见的东西仍可能充满整个房间。

intro.en: The phrase combines a Germanic noun with a Latin one; the Latin element carries most of the derivational family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把日耳曼语名词与拉丁语名词组合在一起，派生词族主要来自拉丁部分。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor gives vapor, vaporize, vaporization, vaporous and vapid; English water supplies watermark, watery and waterlogged.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 衍生 vapor、vaporize、vaporization、vaporous 与 vapid；英语 water 构成 watermark、watery 与 waterlogged。

items.example: The ditch carried water to the field.
Vapor rose from the hot spring.

items.exampleCN: 汽化使剩下的液体降温。

items.example: A vaporous haze hung over the marsh.
items.exampleCN: 沼泽上方悬着一层雾状薄霭。

items.meaningCN: 作定语用的复合修饰语

definition_zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；挥发气体；幻想之物
definition_en: a substance in its gaseous state, especially one given off by a liquid or solid, or a faint mist
core_image: 一滴汽油落在热石头上，转眼化成一缕看不见的气，散进空气
scene: 加油站的地面上洒了一点汽油，太阳晒过后空气里浮起一层薄薄的气。Petrol vapor drifted across the forecourt until the warning sign was moved closer.
sceneCN: 这里指「由液体挥发出来的气体」（第 1 个义项：液体或固体变成的气态物质）；句意为汽油蒸气飘过加油场地，直到警告牌被移近。图中可辨识物件：加油机、湿地面、浮起的气层、警告牌。

pos.zh: 蒸气；水汽；雾气；挥发气体

senses.title: A substance given off as gas
senses.titleCN: 由液体或固体发出的气态物质
senses.definition: the gaseous form of a substance that has passed off from a liquid or solid
senses.definitionCN: 由液体或固体散出后形成的气态物质
senses.example: Petrol vapor drifted across the forecourt until the warning sign was moved closer.
senses.exampleCN: 汽油蒸气飘过加油场地，直到警告牌被移近。
senses.why: Latin vapor named steam and exhalation, so the English word starts from what rises off a warm surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁 vapor 指蒸汽与呼出的气，因此英语这个词从「自温热表面升腾而起的东西」出发。

senses.title: Water as an invisible gas
senses.titleCN: 看不见的水汽
senses.definition: gaseous water, whether in the air or above a warm surface
senses.definitionCN: 处于气态的水，无论在空气中还是在温热表面上方的水
senses.example: The vapour above the kettle is water, not smoke.
senses.exampleCN: 壶上方的气是水汽，不是烟。
senses.why: The commonest vapor in daily life is water, so the word is regularly used without naming the substance.
senses.whyCN: 日常最常见的蒸气就是水，因此这个词常单独使用而不必点明物质。

senses.title: A faint visible mist
senses.titleCN: 肉眼可见的薄雾、气团
senses.definition: a thin mist or cloud of condensed droplets that can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 由凝结液滴构成、能被看见的薄雾或气团
senses.example: A cold vapor hung over the hot spring at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 黎明时温泉上方挂着一层冷雾。
senses.why: Visible vapour is already part liquid, but English kept one word for both the invisible gas and the mist it makes.
senses.whyCN: 可见的蒸气其实已含液态，但英语用同一个词兼指看不见的气与它形成的雾。

senses.title: The gas phase in chemistry
senses.titleCN: 化学与工程中的气相
senses.definition: the gaseous phase of a substance studied apart from its liquid or solid phase
senses.definitionCN: 物质的气相，与液相、固相并列研究
senses.example: The vapour above the solvent reached equilibrium with the liquid.
senses.exampleCN: 溶剂上方的气相与液相达到平衡。
senses.why: Laboratory usage turned the everyday word into a name for one phase in a system of phases.
senses.whyCN: 实验室用法把这个日常词变成物相体系中的一个相名。

senses.title: Fumes from fuel or solvent
senses.titleCN: 燃料或溶剂挥发的气体
senses.definition: the flammable or harmful gas given off by a fuel, solvent or chemical
senses.definitionCN: 燃料、溶剂或化学品散出的易燃或有毒气体
senses.example: Vapour from the tank collected under the shed roof.
senses.exampleCN: 罐中散出的蒸气聚集在棚顶下。
senses.why: Industry applied the word to whatever a liquid gives off, and with it came the language of risk.
senses.whyCN: 工业界用这个词指液体散出的一切气体，随之而来的是风险的语言。

senses.title: The aerosol from an e-cigarette
senses.titleCN: 电子烟产生的气雾
senses.definition: the cloud exhaled from a device that heats a liquid rather than burning tobacco
senses.definitionCN: 由加热液体、而非燃烧烟草的装置呼出的气团
senses.example: A sweet vapor filled the shop's tasting room.
senses.exampleCN: 一股甜味气雾充满店里的试抽室。
senses.why: The newer use stretches the word to a cloud that is mostly droplets, because it looks and behaves like vapour.
senses.whyCN: 较新的用法把这个词扩展到以液滴为主的气团，因为它看上去、动起来都像蒸气。

senses.title: The old medical 'vapours'
senses.titleCN: 旧时医学所说的「体内之气」
senses.definition: in older medicine, exhalations believed to rise from the body and cause low spirits
senses.definitionCN: 旧医学认为自体内升起、引起情绪低落的气
senses.example: The eighteenth-century letter blamed her melancholy on the vapours.
senses.exampleCN: 这封十八世纪的书信把她的忧郁归因于体内之气。
senses.why: Before physiology, illness was often explained by rising vapours, and the plural became a name for melancholy itself.
senses.whyCN: 在生理学之前，疾病常被解释为上升的气，复数形式遂成为「忧郁」的代称。

senses.title: Something without substance
senses.titleCN: 比喻：虚无缥缈之物
senses.definition: something imagined, insubstantial or without practical effect
senses.definitionCN: 想象出来的、没有实体或没有实际作用的东西
senses.example: The promise turned out to be vapor and nothing more.
senses.exampleCN: 那个承诺到头来只是空话。
senses.why: What has no body and cannot be grasped became the natural image for a claim with no substance.
senses.whyCN: 没有形体、抓不住的东西，自然成了「没有实质的主张」的意象。

intro.en: Vapor comes from Latin vapor 'steam, exhalation, warmth', through Old French. It entered English in the late fourteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: vapor 经古法语来自拉丁 vapor「蒸汽、呼气、热」，在十四世纪末进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Vapor covered steam, breath and warmth, and could also mean a light exhalation rising from the ground. The word was used in both everyday and medical writing.
items.cn: vapor 兼指蒸汽、呼吸与热，也可指从地面升起的轻气。这个词在日常写作与医学写作中都出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): vapor has no established pre-Latin origin. Suggestions linking it to vapidus 'flat, spoiled' or to a Greek form are hypotheses, not proven derivations.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：vapor 没有已确定的拉丁语之前来源。把它与 vapidus「走味的、败坏的」或某个希腊形式相联系的说法都是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Old French vapour carried the noun into English, where the spelling vapor later became standard in American use.
items.cn: 古法语 vapour 把这个名词带入英语，后来 vapor 这一拼写成为美式标准。

items.en: From the seventeenth century the plural vapours named a condition of low spirits, thought to arise from exhalations within the body.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，复数 the vapours 指一种情绪低落的状态，时人认为它源于体内升起的气。

items.en: Nineteenth-century physics fixed vapor as a technical term for the gas phase of a substance below its critical temperature.
items.cn: 十九世纪的物理学把 vapor 固定为术语，指低于临界温度时物质的气相。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries added fuel vapour, vapour trails and the aerosol of vaping, all extensions of the same visible or invisible cloud.
items.cn: 二十与二十一世纪又添出燃料蒸气、凝结尾迹与电子烟气雾，都是同一种可见或不可见气团的延伸。

note.en: Group one holds forms of the same word or its near-homographs; group two holds the physical neighbours of vapour in the air.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词的各种形式或近形词；第二组是空气中和蒸气相邻的物理概念。

entries.definition: The identical word in British spelling; only the orthography differs.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，只有正字法不同。

entries.definition: From vapidus 'flat, spoiled', used of drinks and later of dull talk; it is not a form of vapor.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 vapidus「走味的、败坏的」，先用于饮料，后指乏味的言谈；并非 vapor 的词形变化。

entries.definition: e- 'out' plus vaporare: to pass off as vapour, the action rather than the substance.
entries.definitionCN: e-「向外」加 vaporare：以蒸气形式散失，是动作而非物质。

entries.definition: A device that turns a liquid into vapour or spray; the machine, not the gas.
entries.definitionCN: 把液体变成蒸气或喷雾的装置；指机器而非气体。

entries.definition: The hot vapour produced by boiling water, often visible; vapor is the wider term for any gaseous substance.
entries.definitionCN: 沸水产生的热蒸气，常可见；vapor 是泛指任何气态物质的更宽的词。

entries.definition: A suspension of tiny liquid droplets; it is already condensed, while vapour may still be a true gas.
entries.definitionCN: 微小液滴的悬浮体，已经凝结；而 vapor 仍可能是真正的气体。

entries.definition: A gas or smoke that is unpleasant or harmful, usually from a chemical process; vapor is neutral about harm.
entries.definitionCN: 令人不适或有害的气体或烟，通常来自化学过程；vapor 对是否有害保持中立。

entries.definition: The general word for any substance in the gaseous state; vapor is usual for gas given off by a liquid or solid.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指任何气态物质的通用词；vapor 通常指由液体或固体散出的气体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin vapor meant steam and breath, so anything that rises off a warm surface is a vapor.
normal.cn: 拉丁 vapor 意为蒸汽与呼气，因此从温热表面升起的东西都可称 vapor。

normal.en: The family runs vaporize, vaporization, vaporizer, vaporous and evaporate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 vaporize、vaporization、vaporizer、vaporous 与 evaporate。

normal.en: Technical phrases mark the science: vapor pressure, vapor phase, vapor trail.
normal.cn: 技术搭配标出科学义：蒸气压、气相、凝结尾迹。

normal.en: American spelling is vapor; British spelling is vapour, the same word twice.
normal.cn: 美式拼作 vapor，英式拼作 vapour，是同一个词的两种写法。

normal.en: Vapour is invisible as a gas and visible only once it condenses into droplets.
normal.cn: 作为气体时蒸气看不见，一旦凝结成液滴才可见。

abstract.en: Picture a coin left in the sun until nothing solid remains in your hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币晒在太阳下，手里最后什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a promise written on a window that fogs and then clears.
abstract.cn: 想象写在窗上的承诺，起雾又散去。

abstract.en: Picture a breath you can see for a second on a winter morning.
abstract.cn: 想象冬日清晨一口能看见一瞬的呼气。

examples.en: Fuel vapor ignites if a spark reaches the tank vent.
examples.cn: 火花触及油箱通气口时，燃料蒸气会被点燃。

examples.en: The vapour above the solvent was vented through a scrubber.
examples.cn: 溶剂上方的蒸气经洗涤器排出。

examples.en: His plans proved to be vapor once the funding was checked.
examples.cn: 资金一核对，他的计划便成了空话。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「vapor 听起来像『微泼』」——水一泼到热处就化成气 → 蒸气

root: 拉丁 vapor「蒸汽、呼气、热」，经古法语 vapour 进入英语；vapor 在拉丁语之前的来源不确定，与 vapidus「走味的」的联系仅为假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one rising cloud: it is gas given off by matter, it is water, it is a visible mist, it is a phase, it is fuel fume, it is aerosol, it was once a name for melancholy, and at last it is anything with no substance.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一团升起的气展开：它是物质散出的气体，是水，是可见的雾，是一个物相，是燃料气，是气雾，曾是忧郁的代称，最后指一切没有实质之物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drop on hot stone turning into a curl of gas too fine to see.
core.cn: 核心意象：热石上的一滴水化作一缕细得看不见的气。

branches.en: PLAIN SUBSTANCE: water or petrol, the gas comes off a liquid.
branches.cn: 基本物质：无论是水还是汽油，气体都自液体散出。

branches.en: VISIBLE CLOUD: once droplets form, the vapour can be seen.
branches.cn: 可见的气团：液滴一旦形成，蒸气便看得见。

branches.en: ONE PHASE: chemistry names the gas phase beside liquid and solid.
branches.cn: 一个物相：化学把气相与液相、固相并列命名。

branches.en: RISK AND DEVICE: fuel fumes and the aerosol of a heated liquid both fill a space.
branches.cn: 风险与装置：燃料气与加热液体产生的气雾都会充满空间。

branches.en: NO BODY: the old humours and the empty promise share the same thinness.
branches.cn: 没有形体：旧时的体液说与空洞的承诺共享同一种稀薄。

intro.en: Vapor is a Latin noun whose stem builds a whole family of English words for turning into gas and for misty appearance.
intro.cn: vapor 是拉丁名词，其词干在英语中构成一整套表示「变成气体」与「雾状外观」的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin vapor and vaporare give vapor, vaporous, evaporate and evaporation; -ize and -izer are living English suffixes.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 vapor 与 vaporare 衍生 vapor、vaporous、evaporate 与 evaporation；-ize 与 -izer 是仍在使用的英语后缀。

items.example: A vapour rose from the spring.
The hot stone steamed in the rain.
The valley was vaporous at sunrise.
A vaporous haze hung over the town.
items.exampleCN: 一层雾状的薄霭罩着小镇。

definition_zh: 温室效应；大气保温效应；温室内的升温效应
definition_en: the warming of a planet's surface caused by gases in its atmosphere that let sunlight in but hold back outgoing heat
core_image: 一层透明的玻璃罩住菜畦，阳光照进来，热气却出不去
scene: 玻璃花房里阳光直射进来，地面热气被挡在玻璃内侧，温度计一路上升。The greenhouse effect kept the flower house warm long after the sun had gone behind the hill.
sceneCN: 这里指「透明覆盖物让阳光进入、又拦住热量外散所造成的升温」（第 1 个义项：大气或透光层截留长波辐射、使表面升温的机制）；句意为太阳落到山后很久，温室效应仍让花房保持温暖。图中可辨识物件：玻璃屋顶、菜畦、温度计、山影。

pos.zh: 温室效应；大气保温效应

collocations.phrase: the greenhouse effect of the atmosphere
trap heat through the greenhouse effect
collocations.zh: 通过温室效应截住热量

senses.title: Heat held by an atmosphere
senses.titleCN: 大气截留热量所造成的升温
senses.definition: the process by which gases in a planet's atmosphere let short-wave sunlight pass but absorb and return long-wave heat
senses.definitionCN: 行星大气中的气体让短波阳光通过、却吸收并回送长波热量的过程
senses.example: The greenhouse effect kept the flower house warm long after the sun had gone behind the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳落到山后很久，温室效应仍让花房保持温暖。
senses.why: The name borrows the glass house: glass admits light and holds the warmth inside, and the atmosphere does the same with certain gases.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字借自玻璃温室：玻璃让光进入又把热留在里面，大气凭借某些气体也做同样的事。

senses.title: The human strengthening of that process
senses.titleCN: 人为排放导致的温室效应增强
senses.definition: the added warming produced when human emissions raise the concentration of heat-trapping gases
senses.definitionCN: 人类排放提高截热气体浓度后所增加的变暖
senses.example: The enhanced greenhouse effect is what the treaty tries to limit.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约想要限制的正是增强的温室效应。
senses.why: Once the natural mechanism was understood, the same phrase was used for the human addition, usually marked by the word enhanced.
senses.whyCN: 自然机制被理解之后，同一短语便用于人为附加的部分，通常加上「增强的」一词来标记。

senses.title: The literal warming inside a glasshouse
senses.titleCN: 玻璃温室内实际的升温现象
senses.definition: the rise in temperature inside a glass building used for plants, caused by trapped solar heat
senses.definitionCN: 用于栽培植物的玻璃建筑内部因太阳能被截留而升温
senses.example: The greenhouse effect in the old glasshouse was strong enough to ripen figs.
senses.exampleCN: 那座旧玻璃房里的温室效应足以让无花果成熟。
senses.why: This is the original observation, and the scientific term preserves it as a literal sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的观察，科学术语把它保留为一个字面义项。

senses.title: The same mechanism on other planets
senses.titleCN: 其他行星大气上的同类机制
senses.definition: the warming of another planet's surface by its own atmospheric gases
senses.definitionCN: 其他行星表面因其自身大气气体而升温
senses.example: Venus shows how far a greenhouse effect can go.
senses.exampleCN: 金星展示了温室效应能走到多远。
senses.why: Planetary science generalized the earthbound term, since the physics depends on gases and pressure rather than on glass.
senses.whyCN: 行星科学把这个地球上的术语一般化，因为其中的物理取决于气体与气压，而非玻璃。

senses.title: The radiation budget in plain terms
senses.titleCN: 从辐射收支看的过程
senses.definition: the imbalance in which incoming short-wave radiation exceeds outgoing long-wave radiation at the surface
senses.definitionCN: 地表接收的短波辐射多于向外散失的长波辐射这一不平衡
senses.example: The greenhouse effect is a budget statement, not a blanket.
senses.exampleCN: 温室效应是一笔收支账，而不是一条毯子。
senses.why: Physicists restated the everyday image as a balance of incoming and outgoing radiation, and the phrase carried over.
senses.whyCN: 物理学家把日常意象改写为进出辐射的收支，并沿用了这个短语。

senses.title: A trapped and amplified effect
senses.titleCN: 比喻：封闭系统内被放大的效应
senses.definition: any situation in which a closed setting traps something and multiplies its effect
senses.definitionCN: 任何封闭环境把某物截住并放大其作用的局面
senses.example: Online outrage has its own greenhouse effect: heat stays and compounds.
senses.exampleCN: 网络上的愤怒自有其温室效应：热度留存并不断叠加。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps two parts of the original: a boundary that holds, and a build-up that follows from holding.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了原义的两部分：一道拦住的边界，以及因拦住而产生的累积。

senses.title: A shorthand in climate policy
senses.titleCN: 气候政策话语中的简称
senses.definition: a short way of naming the atmospheric mechanism in public and policy discussion
senses.definitionCN: 在公共与政策讨论中称呼大气机制的简便说法
senses.example: The briefing put the greenhouse effect before every other item.
senses.exampleCN: 简报把温室效应排在所有议题之前。
senses.why: Policy needed a compact label that a general audience already knew, so the technical phrase became a shorthand.
senses.whyCN: 政策需要一个公众已经知道的简短标签，于是这个技术短语成了简称。

senses.title: A self-reinforcing warming loop
senses.titleCN: 比喻：使状况不断升温的循环
senses.definition: a feedback loop in which warming causes changes that cause still more warming
senses.definitionCN: 变暖引起变化、变化又引起更多变暖的反馈循环
senses.example: Melting ice creates a greenhouse effect of its own by darkening the ground.
senses.exampleCN: 冰层融化使地面变暗，从而造出它自己的温室效应。
senses.why: The feedback sense pushes the image further: the trapped heat now changes the container so that it traps more.
senses.whyCN: 反馈义把意象再推一步：被截住的热改变了容器，使它截住更多。

intro.en: Greenhouse effect is a modern English compound of greenhouse, a glass building for plants, and effect from Latin effectus 'accomplishment'. The phrase was formed in the nineteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: greenhouse effect 是近代英语复合词，由 greenhouse（栽培植物的玻璃建筑）与来自拉丁 effectus「完成、结果」的 effect 构成。这个短语成形于十九世纪。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greenhouse is an English compound of green 'growing, verdant' and house, naming a glass building where plants are kept warm out of season.
items.cn: greenhouse 是英语复合词，由 green「青绿的、生长的」与 house 构成，指让植物在不当季时也保持温暖的玻璃建筑。

items.en: Effectus 'a doing, accomplishment' came from efficere 'to work out', itself ex- 'out' plus facere 'to do, make'. The noun is the source of English effect.
items.cn: effectus「做成、完成」来自 efficere「做出」，后者由 ex-「向外」加 facere「做、造」构成。这个名词是英语 effect 的来源。

items.en: In the 1820s Fourier described how the atmosphere keeps a planet warmer than its distance from the sun would allow; the glass-house comparison followed and gave the phenomenon its name.
items.cn: 十九世纪二十年代，傅里叶描述了大气如何使行星比按日距推算的更暖；随后出现的玻璃房类比给了这一现象名字。

items.en: The phrase greenhouse effect was current in English by the later nineteenth century and was used alongside the French phrase effet de serre.
items.cn: 到十九世纪后期，greenhouse effect 这一短语已在英语中通行，并与法语 effet de serre 并用。

items.en: Twentieth-century climatology split the natural mechanism from the human enhancement, and both readings now sit inside one phrase.
items.cn: 二十世纪的气候学把自然机制与人为增强分开，而两种读法如今都容在同一个短语里。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first appearance of the English phrase is not firmly dated, though the underlying idea is securely traced to the 1820s. No part of the compound is doubtful in form.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个英语短语的确切首见时间没有定论，但其背后的思想可确凿追溯到十九世纪二十年代。复合词本身的形态并无疑点。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built with greenhouse that look almost the same; group two holds the names of warming processes and quantities.
note.cn: 第一组是同样含 greenhouse、外形几乎相同的短语；第二组是各种变暖过程与相关量的名称。

entries.definition: A gas that traps heat; the effect is what such gases produce together, not the gas itself.
entries.definitionCN: 截住热量的气体；效应是这类气体共同造成的结果，而非气体本身。

entries.definition: The warming attributed to trapped heat, an observed result rather than the mechanism that produces it.
entries.definitionCN: 归因于被截热量的变暖，是观测到的结果而非产生它的机制。

entries.definition: The glass structure that supplied the image; it names a place, not an atmospheric process.
entries.definitionCN: 提供这一意象的玻璃建筑；它指一处场所，而非大气过程。

entries.definition: An occasional synonym built on glasshouse; it never displaced the greenhouse form in scientific use.
entries.definitionCN: 偶尔使用的同义词，以 glasshouse 构词；在科学用法中从未取代 greenhouse 形式。

entries.definition: The measured rise in the earth's average temperature; it is the outcome that the greenhouse effect helps explain.
entries.definitionCN: 地球平均气温的实测上升；它是温室效应所解释的结果。

entries.definition: The change in the energy balance of the climate system, a quantitative measure rather than a named mechanism.
entries.definitionCN: 气候系统能量平衡的改变，是定量指标而非一个有名字的机制。

entries.definition: Local warming over built-up ground; it shares the word effect but has nothing to do with atmospheric gases.
entries.definitionCN: 建筑密集地面上空的局地升温；与 effect 一词共享形式，但与大气气体无关。

entries.definition: Material that slows heat flow; the greenhouse effect works by radiation, not by blocking conduction.
entries.definitionCN: 减缓热流的材料；温室效应靠辐射起作用，而不是阻断传导。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: The name is a comparison: glass admits light and refuses heat, and so does an atmosphere with certain gases.
normal.cn: 这个名字是一个比较：玻璃放光进来、不让热出去，含某些气体的大气亦然。

normal.en: Effect comes from efficere 'to work out', so the phrase says the atmosphere works something out.
normal.cn: effect 来自 efficere「做出」，因此这个短语是说大气「做出」了某个结果。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the readings: natural greenhouse effect, enhanced greenhouse effect, runaway greenhouse effect.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分各种读法：自然温室效应、增强的温室效应、失控的温室效应。

normal.en: The family includes greenhouse, greenhouse gas, greenhouse warming and the adjective effective.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 greenhouse、greenhouse gas、greenhouse warming 与形容词 effective。

normal.en: Venus is the standard example of the mechanism running to extremes.
normal.cn: 金星是该机制走到极端的标准例子。

abstract.en: Picture a car with all its windows shut on a sunny day.
abstract.cn: 想象晴天里车窗全部关着的汽车。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that stays in one room and grows louder each time it is repeated.
abstract.cn: 想象一个传闻留在同一间屋里，每被重复一次就更响。

abstract.en: Picture a blanket that also warms the person who keeps adding layers.
abstract.cn: 想象一条毯子，也给不断加层的人升温。

examples.en: Without any greenhouse effect, the earth's surface would average well below freezing.
examples.cn: 若完全没有温室效应，地表平均温度会远低于冰点。

examples.en: Carbon dioxide strengthens the greenhouse effect by absorbing outgoing infrared radiation.
examples.cn: 二氧化碳吸收向外散出的红外辐射，从而加强温室效应。

examples.en: The students built a box model to show the greenhouse effect in miniature.
examples.cn: 学生们做了一个箱式模型，用缩小的方式演示温室效应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「green（绿）+ house（房子）+ effect（效应）」——玻璃房里菜绿了、热也出不去了 → 温室效应

root: 英语复合词：greenhouse 由 green 与 house 构成，指栽培植物的玻璃房；effect 来自拉丁 effectus「做成、结果」，出自 efficere（ex- + facere）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one comparison: a transparent boundary lets light in and holds heat back, whether the boundary is glass, an atmosphere, another planet's air, a policy label or a closed room of anger.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个比较展开：一道透明边界让光进入、把热拦住，无论这道边界是玻璃、大气、别的行星的空气、一个政策标签，还是一间封闭的怒气之屋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: sunlight enters a glass house, warmth stays inside, the thermometer climbs.
core.cn: 核心意象：阳光进入玻璃房，热量留在里面，温度计上升。

branches.en: MECHANISM: the atmosphere plays the part of glass in a radiation budget.
branches.cn: 机制：大气在辐射收支中扮演玻璃的角色。

branches.en: HUMAN READING: the same phrase names the added part and serves as a policy label.
branches.cn: 人为读法：同一短语指附加的部分，并充当政策标签。

branches.en: LITERAL HOUSE: the glass building is the original observation behind the term.
branches.cn: 字面的房子：玻璃建筑是这个术语背后的最初观察。

branches.en: OTHER WORLDS: the physics travels to any planet with an atmosphere.
branches.cn: 别的世界：这套物理适用于任何有大气层的行星。

branches.en: TRAPPED AND AMPLIFIED: a closed setting holds something until it compounds.
branches.cn: 被截留并放大：封闭环境把某物留住，直到它不断叠加。

intro.en: The phrase is built from two free English words, one Germanic and one Latin-derived, and both bring large families with them.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个自由的英语词构成，一个属日耳曼语来源，一个属拉丁来源，两者都带来大批同族词。

latinIntro.en: Latin facere 'to do' yields effect, effective, efficient, factory and manufacture; greenhouse supplies greenhouse gas and greenhouse warming.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 facere「做」衍生 effect、effective、efficient、factory 与 manufacture；greenhouse 则构成 greenhouse gas 与 greenhouse warming。

items.example: The green shoots appeared in March.
items.exampleCN: 青绿的嫩芽在三月出现。

items.example: The house held the seedlings all winter.
items.exampleCN: 这座房子整冬护着幼苗。

items.example: The effect was visible at once.

items.meaning: in a way that produces results
items.example: The valve effectively sealed the pipe.
items.exampleCN: 阀门有效地封住了管道。

items.meaning: naming the mechanism before a noun
items.exampleCN: 温室效应造成的变暖在全球被测量。

definition_zh: 温室气体；截留热量的气体
definition_en: a gas in the atmosphere that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation and so warms the surface below
core_image: 几只看不见的手在空中把往外跑的热气一把把拦回来
scene: 工厂烟囱上方的空气里混着好几种气，其中几种会把地表散出的热拦住。Every greenhouse gas in the plume was counted before the permit was renewed.
sceneCN: 这里指「能吸收并再辐射红外辐射、使地表升温的气体」（第 1 个义项：大气中截留长波辐射的气体）；句意为在许可证续期之前，烟羽中的每一种温室气体都被核算过。图中可辨识物件：烟囱、烟羽、采样瓶、核算表。

senses.title: A gas that absorbs outgoing infrared radiation
senses.titleCN: 吸收向外红外辐射的气体
senses.definition: an atmospheric gas that absorbs infrared radiation emitted by the surface and re-emits it in all directions
senses.definitionCN: 吸收地表发出的红外辐射并向各方向再辐射的大气气体
senses.example: Every greenhouse gas in the plume was counted before the permit was renewed.
senses.exampleCN: 在许可证续期之前，烟羽中的每一种温室气体都被核算过。
senses.why: The phrase joins the image of a glass house to the physical gas, so the gas is defined by the work the glass was doing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把玻璃房的意象与物理上的气体连在一起，因此这种气体按「玻璃所做的事」来定义。

senses.title: Carbon dioxide as the reference case
senses.titleCN: 作为基准的二氧化碳
senses.definition: carbon dioxide, the gas against which other greenhouse gases are usually compared
senses.definitionCN: 二氧化碳，其他温室气体通常以它为参照
senses.example: Carbon dioxide is the greenhouse gas that dominates the inventory.
senses.exampleCN: 二氧化碳是清单中占主导的温室气体。
senses.why: Because it comes from every fire and is easy to measure, carbon dioxide became the yardstick and often stands for the whole category.
senses.whyCN: 因为凡有燃烧处皆有它、又易于测量，二氧化碳成了标尺，常代表整个类别。

senses.title: Methane from fields and animals
senses.titleCN: 来自农田与牲畜的甲烷
senses.definition: methane, a greenhouse gas released by wetlands, rice fields, livestock and waste
senses.definitionCN: 由湿地、稻田、牲畜与废弃物释放的温室气体甲烷
senses.example: Methane is a greenhouse gas with far more warming power per molecule than carbon dioxide.
senses.exampleCN: 就每个分子而言，甲烷的变暖能力远超二氧化碳。
senses.why: Methane belongs to the category because its molecular bonds absorb infrared strongly, even though it leaves the air quickly.
senses.whyCN: 甲烷属于这一类，是因为其分子键强烈吸收红外，尽管它在大气中停留很短。

senses.title: Nitrous oxide from soil and industry
senses.titleCN: 来自土壤与工业的氧化亚氮
senses.definition: nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas produced by fertilised soil and some industrial processes
senses.definitionCN: 由施过肥的土壤及某些工业过程产生的温室气体氧化亚氮
senses.example: Nitrous oxide is the greenhouse gas most closely tied to fertiliser use.
senses.exampleCN: 氧化亚氮是与化肥使用关系最密切的温室气体。
senses.why: Agriculture made this gas a policy concern, and the category supplied the frame for counting it.
senses.whyCN: 农业使这种气体成为政策关切，而「温室气体」这一类别为核算它提供了框架。

senses.title: The fluorinated industrial gases
senses.titleCN: 含氟的工业温室气体
senses.definition: the synthetic halogenated gases used in refrigeration and industry that trap heat very strongly
senses.definitionCN: 制冷与工业中使用的、截热能力极强的合成卤代气体
senses.example: The fluorinated greenhouse gas leaked from the old cooling plant.
senses.exampleCN: 含氟温室气体从旧的制冷设备中泄漏。
senses.why: These gases exist only because industry made them, yet their behaviour puts them in the same physical class.
senses.whyCN: 这些气体只因工业制造而存在，但它们的行为把其归入同一个物理类别。

senses.title: Water vapor counted as a gas
senses.titleCN: 作为温室气体计入的水汽
senses.definition: gaseous water, which is the most abundant heat-trapping gas although it is not counted as a human emission
senses.definitionCN: 气态水，是含量最多的截热气体，但不作为人为排放核算
senses.example: Water vapor is a greenhouse gas in the strongest sense, yet it is treated as feedback.
senses.exampleCN: 水汽在最强的意义上是温室气体，却被当作反馈来处理。
senses.why: The physical definition includes it, while accounting practice excludes it, and both uses sit inside the same phrase.
senses.whyCN: 物理定义包含它，核算实践排除它，两种用法都容纳在同一短语中。

senses.title: The total load in accounting
senses.titleCN: 核算中的温室气体总量
senses.definition: the aggregate amount of such gases expressed in a common unit such as carbon dioxide equivalent
senses.definitionCN: 这类气体的合计量，以二氧化碳当量等共同单位表示
senses.example: The city's greenhouse gas fell for a third year.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市的温室气体总量连续第三年下降。
senses.why: Governance needs one number, so a countable plural takes the sense of a total burden rather than a gas.
senses.whyCN: 治理需要一个数字，因此可数的复数形式取得「总负担」之义，而不指某一种气体。

senses.title: Anything that traps and amplifies
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何加重某种效应的因素
senses.definition: something that keeps an unwanted effect in place and makes it build up
senses.definitionCN: 使某种不良效应留驻并不断加剧的事物
senses.example: Cheap storage was the greenhouse gas of the whole subsidy scheme.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价的仓储成了整个补贴方案中不断加码的因素。
senses.why: The metaphor drops the chemistry and keeps the function: it holds heat in, and holding makes it worse.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻舍去化学，只保留功能：它把热留住，而留住使它更糟。

intro.en: Greenhouse gas combines the English greenhouse with gas, a word coined in the seventeenth century from Greek chaos. The climate meaning is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: greenhouse gas 把英语 greenhouse 与 gas 组合起来；gas 是十七世纪依据希腊 chaos 造出的词。气候义是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Greenhouse names a glass building for plants; the glass lets light in and holds warmth, which is why it supplied the image for atmospheric warming.
items.cn: greenhouse 指栽培植物的玻璃建筑；玻璃让光进入并保住热量，因此为大气变暖提供了意象。

items.en: Gas was coined in the seventeenth century on Greek khaos 'void, empty space', after Dutch chemist van Helmont's word for an airy substance.
items.cn: gas 是十七世纪依据希腊 khaos「虚空、空旷」造出的词，仿自荷兰化学家范海尔蒙特的用语。

items.en: Gas settled as the name for the third state of matter, and the plural gases became ordinary in technical English.
items.cn: gas 固定为物质第三态的称呼，复数 gases 在技术英语中成为常例。

items.en: From the later twentieth century the compound named gases measured for their infrared absorption, and the plural came to mean an accounted total.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这个复合词指按其红外吸收而被测量的气体，复数形式进而指核算出的总量。

items.en: Treaties and inventories fixed the phrase in law, usually in the form greenhouse gas emissions or greenhouse gas concentration.
items.cn: 条约与清单把这个短语写进法律文本，通常作 greenhouse gas emissions 或 greenhouse gas concentration。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the first use of the compound is not closely dated, though its components are unproblematic. Greek khaos itself has no agreed Indo-European source.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个复合词的首见时间没有确切年代，其成分本身并无疑点。希腊 khaos 自身没有公认的印欧来源。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical phrases that name different pieces of the same topic; group two holds gases and quantities often confused with the category.
note.cn: 第一组是外形几乎相同、却指同一话题不同部分的短语；第二组是易与该类别混淆的气体与量。

entries.definition: The process of warming by trapped radiation; the gas is one ingredient, the effect is the working whole.
entries.definitionCN: 由被截留的辐射造成升温的过程；气体是成分，效应是整体运作。

entries.definition: The warming itself, measured in degrees, rather than the gas that contributes to it.
entries.definitionCN: 变暖本身，以温度计量，而非促成它的气体。

entries.definition: The act or amount of releasing such gases; the gas is the substance, the emission is the release.
entries.definitionCN: 释放这类气体的行为或数量；气体是物质，排放是释放。

entries.definition: The glass structure behind the metaphor, with no atmospheric meaning of its own.
entries.definitionCN: 比喻背后的玻璃建筑，本身没有大气含义。

entries.definition: A single gas that happens to be the most discussed greenhouse gas; it is a member, not the category.
entries.definitionCN: 某一种气体，恰好是被讨论最多的温室气体；它是成员，而非类别。

entries.definition: A substance that harms health or ecosystems directly; a greenhouse gas harms by changing the energy balance.
entries.definitionCN: 直接损害健康或生态的物质；温室气体是通过改变能量平衡来起作用。

entries.definition: Fine particles suspended in air, which mostly cool the surface rather than warm it.
entries.definitionCN: 悬在空中的细微颗粒，多数使地表降温而非升温。

entries.definition: A gas that shields the surface from ultraviolet light; it is also a greenhouse gas but is regulated for a different harm.
entries.definitionCN: 为地表挡住紫外线的气体；它也是温室气体，但因另一种危害而受管制。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Two words, one job: a gas that does what the glass of a greenhouse does.
normal.cn: 两个词，一件事：这种气体做着温室玻璃所做的事。

normal.en: The family runs gas, gases, gaseous, gasify, gasification and gassy.
normal.cn: 同族词有 gas、gases、gaseous、gasify、gasification 与 gassy。

normal.en: The four names to remember are carbon dioxide, methane, nitrous oxide and the fluorinated gases.
normal.cn: 要记住的四类是二氧化碳、甲烷、氧化亚氮与含氟气体。

normal.en: Accounting phrases: greenhouse gas emissions, greenhouse gas inventory, greenhouse gas budget.
normal.cn: 核算搭配：温室气体排放、温室气体清单、温室气体预算。

normal.en: Water vapor is the biggest one physically and is left out of human totals.
normal.cn: 水汽在物理上是最大的一种，却不计入人为总量。

abstract.en: Picture a net that catches only the arrows going out, never the ones coming in.
abstract.cn: 想象一张只拦住向外之箭、不拦向内之箭的网。

abstract.en: Picture a thin coat that is invisible but makes the wearer sweat.
abstract.cn: 想象一件看不见的外套，让穿的人出汗。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour that keeps returning from every direction at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从各个方向同时返回的传闻。

examples.en: Methane is a greenhouse gas that leaves the air within decades.
examples.cn: 甲烷是一种在几十年内就会离开大气的温室气体。

examples.en: The inventory lists every greenhouse gas in carbon dioxide equivalent.
examples.cn: 清单把每种温室气体折算为二氧化碳当量列出。

examples.en: Refrigerants are greenhouse gas with very high warming potential.
examples.cn: 制冷剂是变暖潜势极高的温室气体。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「green（绿）+ house（房子）+ gas（气）」——温室里那层留住热的气 → 温室气体

root: 英语复合词：greenhouse（green + house，玻璃花房）+ gas（十七世纪据希腊 khaos「虚空」造出，指气态物质）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one class of gases: the physical definition, the four families usually named, water vapour inside and outside the accounts, the total written in one unit, and finally any factor that holds an effect in place.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一类气体展开：物理定义，通常点名的四类气体，账内与账外的水汽，折成一个单位的总量，最后指任何把效应留住的因素。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: invisible hands catching the heat that tries to leave the ground.
core.cn: 核心意象：看不见的手把试图离开地表的热一把把拦回。

branches.en: DEFINITION: the class is fixed by what the gas does to infrared radiation.
branches.cn: 定义：这一类由气体对红外辐射的作用而定。

branches.en: NAMED MEMBERS: carbon dioxide, methane and nitrous oxide each occupy one sense.
branches.cn: 点名的成员：二氧化碳、甲烷与氧化亚氮各占一个义项。

branches.en: SYNTHETIC MEMBERS: industrial gases join the class by behaviour, not by origin.
branches.cn: 合成成员：工业气体按行为而非来源归入这一类。

branches.en: INSIDE AND OUTSIDE THE LEDGER: water vapour is physical but uncounted, while the total is counted but has no single gas.
branches.cn: 账内与账外：水汽是物理上的成员却不核算，总量被核算却不指某一种气体。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED FUNCTION: any factor that traps and compounds inherits the image.
branches.cn: 功能转移：任何截留并加剧的因素都继承了这一意象。

intro.en: The phrase joins two free words, and the second one carries an unusually productive family of derivatives.
intro.cn: 这个短语由两个自由词构成，后一个词带有异常丰富的派生词族。

latinIntro.en: Gas is not Latin but Greek in origin; it yields gaseous, gasify, gasification and gassy, while greenhouse yields greenhouse warming and greenhouse effect.
latinIntro.cn: gas 并非拉丁来源而是希腊来源，衍生 gaseous、gasify、gasification 与 gassy；greenhouse 则构成 greenhouse warming 与 greenhouse effect。

items.example: Green leaves filled the glass roof.
The house faced south for light.

items.exampleCN: 这饮料喝起来气泡很多。

items.meaning: naming the gas before a noun
items.example: Greenhouse-gas accounting began in the nineties.
items.exampleCN: 温室气体核算始于九十年代。

definition_zh: 全球变暖；全球气温上升
definition_en: the observed rise in the average temperature of the earth's surface and lower atmosphere
core_image: 一整张世界地图上，温度计的红色液柱依次从北往南抬起
scene: 气象站把世界各地上百年的记录汇总起来，曲线一直往上抬。Global warming shows most clearly in the rising minimum temperatures of winter nights.
sceneCN: 这里指「地球平均气温长期上升的现象」（第 1 个义项：地表与低层大气平均温度的实测上升）；句意为全球变暖在冬夜最低气温的抬升上表现得最清楚。图中可辨识物件：百年记录册、上升曲线、世界地图、温度计。

senses.title: The rise in the earth's mean temperature
senses.titleCN: 地球平均气温的上升
senses.definition: the long-term increase in the average temperature of the earth's surface and lower atmosphere
senses.definitionCN: 地表与低层大气平均温度的长期升高
senses.example: Global warming shows most clearly in the rising minimum temperatures of winter nights.
senses.exampleCN: 全球变暖在冬夜最低气温的抬升上表现得最清楚。
senses.why: Global is from Latin globus 'round mass', naming the whole planet as one body; warming is simply the process of becoming warmer.
senses.whyCN: global 来自拉丁 globus「圆球」，把整个行星当作一个整体；warming 就是变暖的过程。

senses.title: The human-caused share of that rise
senses.titleCN: 人为造成的当代变暖
senses.definition: the part of the temperature rise attributed to human emissions of greenhouse gases
senses.definitionCN: 气温上升中归因于人类温室气体排放的部分
