senses.example: Most of recent global warming is attributed to human activity.
senses.exampleCN: 近年全球变暖的大部分被归因于人类活动。
senses.why: Once scientists separated natural variation from added forcing, the same term carried the human share as its main reading.
senses.whyCN: 科学家把自然波动与外加的强迫分开之后，同一个术语便以人为部分为主要读法。

senses.title: The trend in the instrumental record
senses.titleCN: 观测记录中的升温趋势
senses.definition: the upward trend visible in thermometer records and reconstructed series
senses.definitionCN: 温度计记录与重建序列中可见的上升趋势
senses.example: The graph of global warming bends upward after nineteen eighty.
senses.exampleCN: 全球变暖的曲线在一九八零年之后向上弯曲。
senses.why: The phrase became a name for a curve, not just a condition, because the evidence is a time series.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语成了一条曲线的名字，而不只是一种状况，因为证据本身就是时间序列。

senses.title: Warming of ocean and air together
senses.titleCN: 海洋与大气的整体升温
senses.definition: the heating of the coupled ocean and atmosphere, most of whose extra energy enters the sea
senses.definitionCN: 海洋与大气耦合系统的升温，其中额外能量大部分进入海中
senses.example: Global warming is measured in the ocean as well as at the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 全球变暖不仅在地表测量，也在海洋中测量。
senses.why: The word global does real work here: the system is counted as one, including the water that stores most of the heat.
senses.whyCN: global 一词在此实有所指：整个系统作为一个整体核算，包括储热最多的海水。

senses.title: A named target in climate policy
senses.titleCN: 气候政策中的目标指称
senses.definition: the level of temperature rise that policy aims to limit, as in a target of one and a half degrees
senses.definitionCN: 政策力求限制的升温幅度，如一点五度目标
senses.example: The talks fixed a global warming limit that few expected to meet.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈确定了一个少有人料到能达成的全球变暖上限。
senses.why: Policy turned a measured trend into a number to be bounded, and the phrase supplied the label for that bound.
senses.whyCN: 政策把测得的趋势变成一个要被界定的数字，而这个短语为那条界线提供了名称。

senses.title: The term as used in public argument
senses.titleCN: 公共争论中的用语
senses.definition: the phrase as it functions in public debate, where it can be accepted, disputed or avoided
senses.definitionCN: 这一短语在公共辩论中的作用，可以被接受、质疑或回避
senses.example: The report avoided the words global warming and still described the trend.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告避开了全球变暖这个词，却仍描述了该趋势。
senses.why: A term that names a contested issue becomes itself a move in the argument, so its use carries meaning beyond its definition.
senses.whyCN: 命名争议议题的术语本身就成了论辩中的一步，因此用不用它都带超出定义的含义。

senses.title: A general rise in heat or intensity
senses.titleCN: 比喻：范围广泛的升温
senses.definition: a widespread increase in intensity, excitement or pressure in some activity or place
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动或某个地方在强度、热度或压力上的普遍上升
senses.example: The league's global warming came from three new sponsors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个联赛的热度上升来自三家新赞助商。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the two parts of the term: the rise is real, and it is measured across a whole field rather than one spot.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留术语的两个部分：上升是真实的，而且是在整个范围内而非一处被测量。

senses.title: A slow build-up of tension
senses.titleCN: 比喻：情绪或局势逐渐激化
senses.definition: a gradual increase in tension or emotion that affects a whole group
senses.definitionCN: 影响整个群体的紧张或情绪逐渐升高
senses.example: You could feel the global warming in the room before anyone spoke.
senses.exampleCN: 还没人开口，就能感到屋里的气氛在升温。
senses.why: Here the phrase works as an extended figure, using the planet's scale for a room's mood.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个短语用作扩展的比喻，把行星的尺度借给一间屋子的气氛。

intro.en: Global warming joins global, from Latin globus 'round mass', with warming from the Old English verb wearmian. The phrase is a twentieth-century coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: global warming 把来自拉丁 globus「圆球」的 global 与古英语动词 wearmian 来的 warming 组合在一起。这个短语是二十世纪的造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Globus meant 'a round mass, a ball, a sphere', and also 'a crowd' in some uses. Its deeper origin is uncertain, and any Indo-European root proposed for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: globus 意为「圆块、球、球体」，某些用法中也指「一群人」。其更深来源不确定，为其提出的印欧词根均属重构。

items.en: Globe entered English in the fourteenth century; the adjective global followed much later, formed on globe with -al and meaning 'of the whole world'.
items.cn: globe 在十四世纪进入英语；形容词 global 出现得晚得多，由 globe 加 -al 构成，意为「整个世界的」。

items.en: Warm descends from Old English wearm, with a verb wearmian 'to make warm'; warming is its verbal noun in -ing.
items.cn: warm 出自古英语 wearm，并带动词 wearmian「使暖」；warming 是它加 -ing 构成的动词性名词。

items.en: The phrase global warming was in use by the middle of the twentieth century, as measurements of mean temperature became worldwide rather than local.
items.cn: 到二十世纪中叶，global warming 这一短语已在使用，因为平均温度的测量从局地走向全球。

items.en: From the 1980s the term moved from research papers into treaties and headlines, and a warming limit became a negotiable number.
items.cn: 从二十世纪八十年代起，这个术语从研究论文走进条约与头条，升温上限成了一个可谈判的数字。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date only): the exact first appearance of the English phrase is not firmly fixed, though the underlying measurements date from the same period. No component of the compound is in doubt.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅首见年代）：这个英语短语的确切首见时间没有定论，但相关测量同出这一时期。复合词的各成分并无疑点。

note.en: Group one holds phrases that look nearly identical but name a different object; group two holds the wider and narrower names for the same change.
note.cn: 第一组是外形几乎相同、所指对象不同的短语；第二组是同一变化在更宽与更窄尺度上的名称。

entries.definition: A factor comparing one gas's warming effect with carbon dioxide over a set period; it is a ratio, not a rise in temperature.
entries.definitionCN: 把某种气体的变暖作用与二氧化碳在特定期限内相比较的系数；它是一个比值，而非气温上升。

entries.definition: The temperature rise that policy aims to stay below; the term names a goal rather than the observed trend.
entries.definitionCN: 政策力求不超出的升温幅度；这个词指目标而非观测到的趋势。

entries.definition: The averaged temperature of the whole planet at a given time; warming is the change in that quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 某一时刻整个行星的平均温度；变暖是这个量的变化。

entries.definition: Any long-term change in climate, including rainfall, ice and sea level; warming is only the temperature part.
entries.definitionCN: 气候的任何长期改变，包括降水、冰盖与海平面；变暖只是其中温度的那一部分。

entries.definition: The broader heading under which warming sits, since a warmer average alters wind, rain and ice as well.
entries.definitionCN: 变暖所处的更宽的标题，因为平均变暖也会改变风、雨与冰。

entries.definition: The general act of making something warmer; global warming specifies the scale and the measured subject.
entries.definitionCN: 使某物变暖的一般说法；global warming 指明尺度与被测对象。

entries.definition: The trapping of radiation that drives the rise; warming is the outcome, not the cause.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动升温的辐射截留机制；变暖是结果，而非原因。

entries.definition: The swelling of seawater as it warms, a result of warming rather than warming itself.
entries.definitionCN: 海水受热膨胀，是变暖的结果而非变暖本身。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Global is globus 'ball': the whole ball of the earth is the unit being measured.
normal.cn: global 出自 globus「球」：被测量的是整个地球这个球。

normal.en: Warming is the -ing noun of warm, so the phrase names an ongoing process, not a finished state.
normal.cn: warming 是 warm 加 -ing 的名词，因此短语指进行中的过程，而非已完成的状态。

normal.en: The family runs globe, global, globally, globalize, globalization, warm, warmth and warmer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 globe、global、globally、globalize、globalization、warm、warmth 与 warmer。

normal.en: Policy phrases: global warming target, global warming potential, slow global warming.
normal.cn: 政策搭配：全球变暖目标、全球变暖潜势、减缓全球变暖。

normal.en: The clearest signs are winter minimum temperatures and ocean heat content.
normal.cn: 最清楚的迹象是冬夜最低气温与海洋热含量。

abstract.en: Picture a whole map blushing at once rather than one town.
abstract.cn: 想象整张地图一起泛红，而不是一个小镇。

abstract.en: Picture a room where everyone speaks a little louder each minute.
abstract.cn: 想象一间屋子，每个人每分钟都说得更响一点。

abstract.en: Picture a kettle that has not yet whistled but is already too hot to hold.
abstract.cn: 想象一只还没鸣叫、却已烫得拿不住的水壶。

examples.en: Global warming lengthens the growing season in some northern regions.
examples.cn: 全球变暖延长了某些北方地区的生长季。

examples.en: The class debated whether global warming should be called a crisis.
examples.cn: 课堂上争论全球变暖是否该被称为危机。

examples.en: Methane's global warming potential is far above that of carbon dioxide.
examples.cn: 甲烷的全球变暖潜势远高于二氧化碳。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「global（全球）+ warming（变暖）」——整个地球一起变热 → 全球变暖

root: 英语复合词：global 来自拉丁 globus「圆球」，加 -al；warming 来自古英语 wearm「暖」的动词 wearmian 加 -ing。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one measured rise: the planet's mean warms, people are named as its cause, the record shows a trend, the ocean joins in, policy fixes a limit, public argument uses the label, and at last any field or room can warm as a whole.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次被测的上升展开：行星均温升高，人被指为其原因，记录显出趋势，海洋也加入，政策定出上限，公共论辩使用这个标签，最后任何领域或房间都能整体升温。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: red columns on a world map rising year after year.
core.cn: 核心意象：世界地图上的红色液柱年复一年地上升。

branches.en: THE WHOLE PLANET: surface and ocean are counted as one warming body.
branches.cn: 整个行星：地表与海洋被算作同一个升温体。

branches.en: CAUSE AND TREND: the human share is separated, and the record makes the rise a curve.
branches.cn: 原因与趋势：人为部分被分开，记录使上升成为曲线。

branches.en: POLICY AND ARGUMENT: a trend becomes a bound, and the label itself becomes a move in debate.
branches.cn: 政策与论辩：趋势变成界线，标签本身成了论辩中的一步。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED SCALE: any field can heat up across its whole extent.
branches.cn: 尺度转移：任何领域都能整体热起来。

branches.en: A ROOM WARMS: the planetary figure shrinks to a mood in one room.
branches.cn: 一室升温：行星的比喻缩成一间屋子的气氛。

intro.en: Both words are free English forms, one from Latin and one from Old English, and each carries a set of common derivatives.
intro.cn: 两个词都是自由的英语形式，一个来自拉丁语，一个来自古英语，各自带有一套常见派生词。

latinIntro.en: Latin globus yields globe, global, globally, globalize and globalization; the Germanic warm gives warmth, warmer and warmest.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 globus 衍生 globe、global、globally、globalize 与 globalization；日耳曼来源的 warm 给出 warmth、warmer 与 warmest。

items.example: The globe stood on the desk.
A global view takes in the whole earth.
items.exampleCN: 全球视角纳入整个地球。
全球贸易把各港口连起来。
这种气体在全球范围内被测量。

items.example: The warmth lingered in the stones.
This winter is warmer than the last.

items.exampleCN: 变暖在几十年前就开始了。

definition_zh: 气候变化；气候变迁；大环境的转变
definition_en: a lasting change in the patterns of temperature, rainfall and wind, especially the change caused by human emissions
core_image: 一本翻了几十年的气象记录，雨量与温度两行都慢慢改了模样
scene: 老农翻着祖父留下的雨量簿，发现同一块田的雨季一年年往后推。Climate change had shifted the rains so far that the sowing calendar no longer matched the sky.
sceneCN: 这里指「气候型态在长期尺度上的改变」（第 1 个义项：气温、降水、风等气候统计特征持续改变）；句意为气候变化把雨季推得太远，播种日历已对不上天时。图中可辨识物件：雨量簿、日历、田垄、云层。

senses.title: A lasting shift in climate statistics
senses.titleCN: 气候统计特征的长期改变
senses.definition: a lasting change in the statistical patterns of temperature, precipitation and wind over decades or longer
senses.definitionCN: 气温、降水与风等统计型态在数十年或更长时间尺度上的持续改变
senses.example: Climate change had shifted the rains so far that the sowing calendar no longer matched the sky.
senses.exampleCN: 气候变化把雨季推得太远，播种日历已对不上天时。
senses.why: Climate is from Greek klima 'slope, zone', the belt of weather a place is inclined toward; change adds Latin cambiare 'to exchange', so the phrase names an exchange of one pattern for another.
senses.whyCN: climate 来自希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」，指某地倾向的天气带；change 添上拉丁 cambiare「交换」，因此短语指一种型态换成了另一种。

senses.title: The present human-driven change
senses.titleCN: 当代人为驱动的气候变化
senses.definition: the current global change in climate attributed mainly to greenhouse gas emissions
senses.definitionCN: 当前全球气候的改变，主要归因于温室气体排放
senses.example: Climate change is now the default reading of the phrase in news reports.
senses.exampleCN: 在新闻报道中，气候变化如今是这个短语的默认读法。
senses.why: Because one instance of the general phenomenon became urgent, the bare phrase came to mean that instance.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个一般现象中的某一例变得紧迫，光秃秃的短语便转而指那一例。

senses.title: Change on a geological timescale
senses.titleCN: 地质尺度上的气候变迁
senses.definition: climate shifts reconstructed over thousands or millions of years from ice, rock and sediment
senses.definitionCN: 从冰芯、岩石与沉积物重建的数千至数百万年尺度的气候改变
senses.example: Ice cores record climate change across the last glacial cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 冰芯记录了上一个冰期旋回中的气候变迁。
senses.why: The phrase is older than the current concern: geology used it for any lasting shift, with no human agent implied.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语比当下的忧患更早：地质学用它指任何持久改变，并不含人为施动者。

senses.title: A regional shift in a single climate
senses.titleCN: 某一地区气候的改变
senses.definition: a change in the climate of one region, such as a wetter monsoon or a shorter cold season
senses.definitionCN: 某个地区气候的改变，如更湿的季风或更短的冷季
senses.example: Climate change in the highlands has shortened the frost season.
senses.exampleCN: 高原地区的气候变化缩短了霜期。
senses.why: The phrase works at any scale, since climate itself is a regional notion before it is a planetary one.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语适用于任何尺度，因为气候在被当作行星概念之前，先是地区性的概念。

senses.title: The object of mitigation policy
senses.titleCN: 减缓政策所针对的对象
senses.definition: the change as something to be slowed by cutting emissions and by managing land and industry
senses.definitionCN: 作为需要通过削减排放、管理土地与工业来减缓的变化
senses.example: Climate change mitigation costs less than repeated disaster relief.
senses.exampleCN: 减缓气候变化的成本低于反复的灾害救助。
senses.why: Policy split the topic in two: mitigation acts on the cause, and the phrase names what is being slowed.
senses.whyCN: 政策把议题一分为二：减缓作用于原因，而这个短语指被减缓的那个变化。

senses.title: The object of adaptation policy
senses.titleCN: 适应政策所针对的对象
senses.definition: the change as something to be lived with through new crops, defences and planning
senses.definitionCN: 作为需要通过新作物、防护与规划来共处的变化
senses.example: Climate change adaptation built the new sea wall higher than the old one.
senses.exampleCN: 为适应气候变化，新海堤修得比旧堤更高。
senses.why: The other half of policy treats the change as a condition rather than a cause, and the same phrase serves both halves.
senses.whyCN: 政策的另一半把这个变化当作条件而非原因，而同一个短语同时服务这两半。

senses.title: A heading in international law
senses.titleCN: 国际法律框架中的用语
senses.definition: the formal label used in treaties and institutions for the issue as a whole
senses.definitionCN: 条约与机构中用来指整个议题的正式标签
senses.example: The protocol fixed climate change as a matter of common concern.
senses.exampleCN: 该议定书把气候变化定为一件事关共同关切的事项。
senses.why: Legal language needs a stable label that covers causes, impacts and obligations at once, which the bare phrase provides.
senses.whyCN: 法律语言需要一个能同时覆盖原因、影响与义务的稳定标签，而这个简洁短语正好提供。

senses.title: A shift in the wider environment
senses.titleCN: 比喻：大环境的转变
senses.definition: a broad shift in conditions surrounding an activity, group or market
senses.definitionCN: 某项活动、群体或市场所处条件的广泛转变
senses.example: The industry felt a climate change of its own as tariffs fell.
senses.exampleCN: 关税下降时，这个行业感到了自己的气候变化。
senses.why: Climate had long been used figuratively for the prevailing mood, so the compound transfers whole to any atmosphere that alters.
senses.whyCN: climate 早已被比喻使用，指当下流行的氛围，因此这个复合词整体转指任何改变中的环境。

intro.en: Climate change joins Greek klima 'slope, zone' with Latin cambiare 'to exchange'. Both parts entered English through French. The compound is modern. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climate change 把希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」与拉丁 cambiare「交换」组合在一起，两个成分都经法语进入英语。复合词是近代的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Klima meant 'a slope, an inclination', and from that 'a zone of the earth' defined by the sun's angle. The word came to mean the weather typical of such a zone.
items.cn: klima 意为「倾斜、倾向」，由此指按太阳角度划分的「地带」，再引申为这一带典型的天气。

items.en: Klima was formed on klinein 'to slope, lean'. The verb belongs to a well-attested Greek family; the noun's shift from slope to zone to weather is a chain of metaphors.
items.cn: klima 由 klinein「倾斜、倚靠」构成。这个动词属于证据充分的希腊词族；名词从「倾斜」到「地带」再到「天气」，是一串比喻的推移。

items.en: Cambiare 'to exchange, barter' is the source of change. Its own origin is uncertain; the suggestion of a Gaulish loan is a hypothesis, not a demonstrated derivation.
items.cn: cambiare「交换、以物易物」是 change 的来源。它自身的来源不确定；「借自高卢语」的说法只是假说，并非已证实的派生。

items.en: Climate entered English in the fourteenth century meaning a zone or region; the weather sense grew through the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.
items.cn: climate 在十四世纪进入英语，意为地带或地区；天气义在十六、十七世纪逐步形成。

items.en: Nineteenth-century geology used climate change for shifts read from strata, with no reference to human causes.
items.cn: 十九世纪的地质学用 climate change 指从地层读出的变迁，不涉及人为原因。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of cambiare is unsettled, and its link to a Celtic form is a hypothesis. The compound's first date is only approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：cambiare 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，与某种凯尔特语形式的联系只是假说。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and phrases built on climate that are easily swapped; group two holds the neighbouring terms for warming and for long-term shifts.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 climate 构成、容易互换的复合词与短语；第二组是变暖与长期变迁方面的近邻术语。

entries.definition: Short-term or periodic fluctuation around a mean, which happens without the mean itself moving.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕均值的短期或周期波动，均值本身并未移动。

entries.definition: A numerical simulation of the climate; a model is what scientists use to project change.
entries.definitionCN: 气候的数值模拟；模式是科学家用来预估变化的工具。

entries.definition: The set of measures adopted in response to the issue; the phrase names actions, not the change itself.
entries.definitionCN: 为应对该议题而采取的一套措施；它指行动而非变化本身。

entries.definition: A shift in day-to-day conditions; weather changes hourly while climate change lasts decades.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日条件的改变；天气逐时变化，而气候变化持续数十年。

entries.definition: The rise in mean temperature alone; climate change also covers rain, ice, sea level and wind.
entries.definitionCN: 仅指平均气温的上升；climate change 还涵盖雨、冰、海平面与风。

entries.definition: A neutral term for a move from one climate state to another, common in geology and palaeontology.
entries.definitionCN: 指从一种气候状态转到另一种的中性说法，常用于地质学与古生物学。

entries.definition: Change in any earth system, including biodiversity and land use; climate is one component.
entries.definitionCN: 任何地球系统的变化，包括生物多样性与土地利用；气候只是其中一项。

entries.definition: The radiative process that drives part of the change; the effect is a cause, the change is a result.
entries.definitionCN: 驱动部分变化的辐射过程；效应是原因，变化是结果。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Klima was a slope: the sun's angle gave each zone its weather, and the zone took the name of its weather.
normal.cn: klima 原指斜面：太阳角度给了每个地带天气，而地带便取了天气之名。

normal.en: Change is cambiare 'to exchange', so the phrase says one climate pattern has been exchanged for another.
normal.cn: change 是 cambiare「交换」，因此短语是说一种气候型态被换成了另一种。

normal.en: The family runs climate, climatic, change, changeable, exchange and exchangeable.
normal.cn: 同族词有 climate、climatic、change、changeable、exchange 与 exchangeable。

normal.en: The two policy halves are fixed phrases: climate change mitigation and climate change adaptation.
normal.cn: 政策的两半是固定搭配：气候变化减缓与气候变化适应。

normal.en: In geology the phrase needs no human cause; in the news it almost always implies one.
normal.cn: 在地质学中这个短语不含人为原因；在新闻中它几乎总暗示人为原因。

abstract.en: Picture a farmer's notebook whose rain columns drift year by year.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农人的账簿，雨量那一栏逐年漂移。

abstract.en: Picture a market whose weather changes while the stalls stay in place.
abstract.cn: 想象一个市场，摊位没动而天气变了。

abstract.en: Picture a house where the rules slowly change and nobody announces it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座房子，规矩慢慢改变而无人宣告。

examples.en: Climate change is altering the timing of spring floods in the Alps.
examples.cn: 气候变化正在改变阿尔卑斯山春汛的时间。

examples.en: The course separates natural climate change from the human-driven kind.
examples.cn: 这门课把自然的气候变迁与人为驱动的那一类分开。

examples.en: Adaptation to climate change costs less than rebuilding after each storm.
examples.cn: 适应气候变化的成本低于每场风暴后的重建。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「climate（气候）+ change（改变）」——气候的型态换了模样 → 气候变化

root: 英语复合词：climate 来自希腊 klima「倾斜、地带」（出自 klinein「倾斜」），经拉丁与法语入英语；change 来自拉丁 cambiare「交换」，其更深来源存疑。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one pattern being exchanged for another: the statistical shift, the present human case, the geological record, the regional version, the two policy faces, the legal label, and finally any surrounding atmosphere that alters.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿「一种型态被换成另一种」展开：统计上的改变，当下的自人为个案，地质记录，地区版本，政策的两个面向，法律标签，最后指任何改变中的周遭氛围。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old rain ledger whose columns no longer match the sky.
core.cn: 核心意象：一本旧雨量簿，上面的数字已与天色对不上。

branches.en: STATISTICS AT ANY SCALE: a region or a planet can shift its averages.
branches.cn: 任何尺度的统计：一个地区或一颗行星都能改变均值。

branches.en: THE PRESENT CASE: one urgent instance takes over the bare phrase.
branches.cn: 当下的个案：一个紧迫的例子占据了这简洁短语。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: geology reads the same phrase without a human agent.
branches.cn: 深时：地质学用同一短语而不含人为施动者。

branches.en: TWO POLICY FACES: slow the cause, or live with the condition.
branches.cn: 政策的两个面向：减缓原因，或与条件共处。

branches.en: LABEL AND METAPHOR: law fixes the phrase, and ordinary speech borrows it for any altered atmosphere.
branches.cn: 标签与比喻：法律固定这个短语，日常言语借它指任何改变的氛围。

intro.en: Both halves are borrowings that became productive English words, so the compound can be read through either family.
intro.cn: 两半都是借入后成为能产英语词的成分，因此复合词可从任一词族来读。

latinIntro.en: Greek klima yields climate, climatic and acclimatize; Latin cambiare yields change, changeable, exchange and interchange.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊 klima 衍生 climate、climatic 与 acclimatize；拉丁 cambiare 衍生 change、changeable、exchange 与 interchange。

items.example: The zone had a mild klima.

items.meaning: the weather typical of a region

items.example: The team acclimatized before the climb.
items.exampleCN: 队伍在登山前适应了气候。

items.meaning: to trade one thing for another

items.example: The two routes interchange at the bridge.

items.meaning: naming the issue before a noun
items.exampleCN: 气候变化政策涵盖两个面向。
