clima, climatis (n., third declension, from Greek)

definition_zh: 碳排放；二氧化碳排放；碳排放量
definition_en: the release of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, especially from burning fuel, or the amount so released
core_image: 一根烟囱把看不见的碳气送进天空，旁边是一本逐日累加的账
scene: 工厂换了新锅炉，烟囱口的气体被采样管接住，工程师把数字记进表格。The retrofit cut the plant's carbon emission by nearly a third.
sceneCN: 这里指「向大气释放二氧化碳」（第 1 个义项：燃烧或工业过程把二氧化碳排入大气）；句意为这次改造使该厂的碳排放减少了近三分之一。图中可辨识物件：烟囱、采样管、记录表、锅炉。

senses.title: Releasing carbon dioxide into the air
senses.titleCN: 把二氧化碳释放到大气中
senses.definition: the act of releasing carbon dioxide into the atmosphere, mainly by burning fuel
senses.definitionCN: 把二氧化碳排入大气，主要来自燃料燃烧
senses.example: The retrofit cut the plant's carbon emission by nearly a third.
senses.exampleCN: 这次改造使该厂的碳排放减少了近三分之一。
senses.why: Carbon is Latin carbo 'charcoal', and emission is Latin emissio 'a sending out'. Together they name carbon sent out as gas.
senses.whyCN: carbon 是拉丁 carbo「木炭」，emission 是拉丁 emissio「送出」，两者合起来指以气体形式送出的碳。

senses.title: The amount released, counted
senses.titleCN: 被核算的排放量
senses.definition: the measured quantity of carbon dioxide released over a period by a source
senses.definitionCN: 某一来源在一段时间内释放的二氧化碳的测量量
senses.example: The city reports its carbon emission every spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市每年春天公布其碳排放量。
senses.why: Since the noun can name a count as well as an act, carbon emission often appears with a number, a target or a year.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个名词既可指动作也可指计数，carbon emission 常与数字、目标或年份连用。

senses.title: The share from burning fossil fuel
senses.titleCN: 来自化石燃料燃烧的排放
senses.definition: the carbon dioxide released by burning coal, oil or gas
senses.definitionCN: 燃烧煤、石油或天然气所释放的二氧化碳
senses.example: Coal still accounts for most of the region's carbon emission.
senses.exampleCN: 煤仍占该地区碳排放的大部分。
senses.why: Chemistry puts the carbon in the fuel and the oxygen in the air, so burning unites them and sends the result up the flue.
senses.whyCN: 化学上碳在燃料里、氧在空气里，燃烧把它们合起来，产物便顺着烟道升走。

senses.title: The share from industrial process
senses.titleCN: 工业过程产生的排放
senses.definition: carbon dioxide released by chemical reactions such as cement making or steel smelting, not by fuel alone
senses.definitionCN: 水泥制造、炼钢等化学反应释放的二氧化碳，不只是燃料产生的
senses.example: Cement kilns produce carbon emission even when their fuel is switched.
senses.exampleCN: 即使更换燃料，水泥窑仍会产生碳排放。
senses.why: Some industries release carbon locked in the raw material, so the phrase covers process chemistry as well as combustion.
senses.whyCN: 有些工业释放锁在原料里的碳，因此这个短语除燃烧外还涵盖工艺化学。

senses.title: The share from changed land use
senses.titleCN: 土地利用变化引起的排放
senses.definition: carbon dioxide released when forest, peat or soil is cleared or drained
senses.definitionCN: 森林、泥炭或土壤被清除或排干时释放的二氧化碳
senses.example: Drained peatland adds a carbon emission that no chimney shows.
senses.exampleCN: 排干的泥炭地带来一种烟囱上看不见的碳排放。
senses.why: The word carbon was extended to the gas released by disturbed ecosystems, since the element is the same wherever it leaves.
senses.whyCN: carbon 一词被扩展到受扰动生态系统中释放的气体，因为无论从哪里逸出，元素都是同一种。

senses.title: The figure used in footprints and ledgers
senses.titleCN: 碳足迹与台账中的数字
senses.definition: the figure assigned to a product, person or institution in carbon accounting
senses.definitionCN: 碳核算中分配给产品、个人或机构的数值
senses.example: The label lists the carbon emission of each shipment.
senses.exampleCN: 标签列出每批货运的碳排放。
senses.why: Accounting turns the physical release into a number attached to an owner, and the phrase follows the number.
senses.whyCN: 核算把物理上的释放变成一个挂在某个主体名下的数字，而这个短语随数字走。

senses.title: The thing that trading schemes cap
senses.titleCN: 交易体系所设上限的对象
senses.definition: the release as a regulated unit that can be capped, priced and traded
senses.definitionCN: 作为可设限、定价与交易的受管制单位
senses.example: Each installation received an allowance for its carbon emission.
senses.exampleCN: 每套装置就其碳排放获得一份配额。
senses.why: Once law defines an allowance per unit of gas, the emission itself becomes a commodity with a quantity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦法律按每单位气体规定配额，排放本身就成了一种有数量的商品。

senses.title: Any harmful discharge
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何有害物的排出
senses.definition: a figurative use for any undesirable output that a system releases into its surroundings
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指系统向周围放出的任何不良产物
senses.example: The department's carbon emission is the paperwork nobody reads.
senses.exampleCN: 这个部门的「碳排放」是那些没人读的文书。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps two features: the output is invisible to the producer, and it accumulates somewhere else.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留两个特征：产物对制造者不可见，却在他处积累。

intro.en: Carbon emission joins Latin carbo 'charcoal' with Latin emissio 'a sending out', from emittere 'to send forth'. The climate sense is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: carbon emission 把拉丁 carbo「木炭」与拉丁 emissio「送出」组合起来，后者出自 emittere「送出」。气候义是二十世纪的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Carbo meant 'charcoal, ember' and gave the element its name. Its deeper origin is uncertain; it may be related to a root for burning, but no such link is proven.
items.cn: carbo 意为「木炭、炭火」，并给了这个元素名称。其更深来源不确定；可能与某个表示「燃烧」的词根有关，但此联系未获证实。

items.en: Emittere 'to send forth' is ex- 'out' plus mittere 'to send'. Mittere has a secure Latin history and gives mission, transmit and permit.
items.cn: emittere「送出」是 ex-「向外」加 mittere「送」。mittere 有可靠的拉丁语历史，衍生 mission、transmit 与 permit。

items.en: Emissio 'a sending out' named the act, and English emission took both the act and the thing sent.
items.cn: emissio「送出」指这一动作，英语 emission 兼指动作与送出的东西。

items.en: Carbon was fixed as the element's name in the late eighteenth century, and emission was applied to gases leaving a process.
items.cn: carbon 在十八世纪后期固定为这个元素的名称，emission 被用于工艺过程中逸出的气体。

items.en: From the later twentieth century the pair became a unit of policy, counted per country, per product and per allowance.
items.cn: 从二十世纪后期起，这一对词成了政策的单位，按国家、按产品、按配额核算。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of carbo is unsettled and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction. The compound's first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：carbo 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，为其提出的任何印欧形式均属重构。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on carbon that look alike but count different things; group two holds the wider vocabulary of releases and of climate accounting.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 carbon 构成、外形相近但核算对象不同的短语；第二组是排放与气候核算中更宽的词汇。

entries.tag: a total attributed to a subject
entries.definition: The total emissions attributed to a person, product or activity; it is a sum, while a single emission is one release.
entries.definitionCN: 归到某个人、产品或活动名下的排放总量；它是总和，而单次排放是一次释放。

entries.definition: The gas itself; carbon emission names its release rather than its chemistry.
entries.definitionCN: 气体本身；carbon emission 指它的释放，而非其化学性质。

entries.definition: A reservoir that absorbs more carbon than it releases, the mirror image of an emission.
entries.definitionCN: 吸收多于释放的碳库，是排放的镜像。

entries.definition: A reduction elsewhere used to balance an emission here; the offset is a credit, not the release.
entries.definitionCN: 在别处取得的减排用来抵销此处的排放；抵销是额度，而非释放。

entries.definition: The release of any heat-trapping gas, including methane and nitrous oxide; carbon emission covers only carbon dioxide.
entries.definitionCN: 任何截热气体的释放，包括甲烷与氧化亚氮；carbon emission 只涵盖二氧化碳。

entries.definition: The gas leaving an engine or pipe; it is the visible stream, while emission is the accounted release.
entries.definitionCN: 离开发动机或管道的气体；它是可见的气流，而 emission 是被核算的释放。

entries.definition: The release of waste into water or air, often regulated for toxicity rather than for warming.
entries.definitionCN: 把废物排入水或空气，常按毒性而非变暖来管制。

entries.definition: Contamination that damages health or ecosystems; carbon dioxide is not a pollutant in the ordinary toxic sense.
entries.definitionCN: 损害健康或生态的污染；二氧化碳并非通常意义上的有毒污染物。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Carbo was charcoal, and emissio was a sending out: the charcoal's element is sent up the flue.
normal.cn: carbo 是木炭，emissio 是送出：木炭中的元素被送出烟道。

normal.en: The family runs carbon, carbonate, carbonated, emit, emission and emissive.
normal.cn: 同族词有 carbon、carbonate、carbonated、emit、emission 与 emissive。

normal.en: Accounting phrases: carbon emission target, carbon emission trading, carbon emission intensity.
normal.cn: 核算搭配：碳排放目标、碳排放交易、碳排放强度。

normal.en: Burning is the usual source: coal, oil and gas each send carbon into the air.
normal.cn: 最常见的来源是燃烧：煤、石油与天然气都把碳送进空气。

normal.en: A sink takes carbon in; an emission sends it out. The two words are opposites.
normal.cn: 碳汇把碳收进去，排放把碳送出去，两者正好相反。

abstract.en: Picture a chimney you cannot see, feeding a cloud nobody owns.
abstract.cn: 想象一根看不见的烟囱，喂养一朵无人拥有的云。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where each page adds a little more weight.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，每翻一页都多一点重量。

abstract.en: Picture a room's litter swept under a rug that keeps rising.
abstract.cn: 想象屋里的碎屑被扫到地毯下，地毯越鼓越高。

examples.en: The steelworks reports its carbon emission monthly to the regulator.
examples.cn: 这家钢厂每月向监管机构报告其碳排放。

examples.en: Switching the fuel cut carbon emission without changing output.
examples.cn: 更换燃料在不改变产量的情况下削减了碳排放。

examples.en: Per capita carbon emission varies widely between the two provinces.
examples.cn: 两省的人均碳排放差别很大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「carbon（碳）+ emission（排放）」——碳被送进空气 → 碳排放

root: 英语复合词：carbon 来自拉丁 carbo「木炭」，更深来源存疑；emission 来自拉丁 emissio「送出」，出自 emittere（ex- + mittere「送」）。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one release: carbon dioxide leaves a fire, a kiln, a drained field or a product chain, is written down as a number, is capped by law, and finally any invisible output can borrow the name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次释放展开：二氧化碳从炉火、窑炉、排干的田地或产品链中逸出，被写成数字，被法律设限，最后任何看不见的产物都能借用这个名字。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chimney sending invisible carbon into the sky while a ledger adds it up.
core.cn: 核心意象：烟囱把看不见的碳送进天空，而账本把它累加。

branches.en: ACT AND AMOUNT: one noun covers the release and the figure counted.
branches.cn: 动作与数量：一个名词兼指释放与被核算的数字。

branches.en: THREE SOURCES: combustion, process chemistry and disturbed land each send the same element up.
branches.cn: 三个来源：燃烧、工艺化学与受扰土地都把同一种元素送上去。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: a physical release becomes an owned number in footprints and accounts.
branches.cn: 台账：物理释放成了有主的数字，进入足迹与账目。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED OUTPUT: any invisible discharge can be called an emission.
branches.cn: 产物转移：任何看不见的排出都可称作排放。

branches.en: THE CAP: the traded unit that schemes set a ceiling on.
branches.cn: 设限对象：交易体系为其设定上限的那个单位。

intro.en: Both halves are Latin loans whose stems build large English families, one chemical and one about sending.
intro.cn: 两半都是拉丁借词，其词干在英语中构成大词族，一个属化学，一个属「送出」。

latinIntro.en: Latin carbo gives carbon, carbonate, carbonic and carbonize; mittere gives emit, emission, mission, transmit and permit.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 carbo 衍生 carbon、carbonate、carbonic 与 carbonize；mittere 衍生 emit、emission、mission、transmit 与 permit。

items.example: The lamp emits a faint glow.

items.meaning: a sending out; that which is sent

items.exampleCN: 这次任务把样品送回家。

definition_zh: 气候变率；气候的自然波动；气候的年际起伏
definition_en: the way climate statistics rise and fall around a mean over seasons, years or decades, apart from any long-term trend
core_image: 一条上下起伏的线，画在一张平直的趋势线旁边，起伏不等于走势
scene: 气象站的记录本上，同一片草原的雨量每年高低起伏，却看不出方向。Year-to-year climate variability hid the slow trend from the farmers.
sceneCN: 这里指「气候统计量围绕均值上下起伏的程度」（第 1 个义项：季节、年际或年代际尺度上气候围绕均值的波动）；句意为年际的气候变率把缓慢的趋势遮住，使农人看不出来。图中可辨识物件：记录本、起伏的雨量曲线、草原、趋势线。

senses.title: Fluctuation of climate around a mean
senses.titleCN: 气候围绕均值的起伏
senses.definition: the range and rhythm of fluctuation in climate statistics around their average, at seasonal to decadal scales
senses.definitionCN: 气候统计量围绕其平均值波动的幅度与节律，尺度从季节到年代际
senses.example: Year-to-year climate variability hid the slow trend from the farmers.
senses.exampleCN: 年际的气候变率把缓慢的趋势遮住，使农人看不出来。
senses.why: Climate is Greek klima 'zone, slope'; variability comes from Latin variare 'to vary', built on varius 'diverse, mottled'. The phrase therefore names how a climate's numbers mottle around their mean.
senses.whyCN: climate 是希腊 klima「地带、斜面」；variability 来自拉丁 variare「变化」，由 varius「杂色的、多样的」构成。因此这个短语指气候的数字如何围绕均值呈现斑驳起伏。

senses.title: Natural fluctuation without an external push
senses.titleCN: 没有外来推动的自然波动
senses.definition: fluctuation generated inside the climate system itself, as by ocean and atmosphere interacting
senses.definitionCN: 由气候系统内部自身产生、如海气相互作用引起的波动
senses.example: Natural climate variability alone cannot explain the last four decades.
senses.exampleCN: 仅凭自然气候变率无法解释最近四十年。
senses.why: Researchers needed to separate the system's own jitter from the response to forcing, and marked the first with the word natural.
senses.whyCN: 研究者需要把系统自身的抖动与对外加强迫的响应分开，并用「自然的」一词标出前者。

senses.title: Year-to-year swings
senses.titleCN: 年际的摆动
senses.definition: changes from one year to the next, such as a wet year followed by a dry one
senses.definitionCN: 从一年到下一年的变化，如湿年之后跟着干年
senses.example: Climate variability from year to year decides whether the reservoir refills.
senses.exampleCN: 年际的气候变率决定水库能否重新蓄满。
senses.why: The scale marker year-to-year narrows the general idea to the interval farmers and water managers actually watch.
senses.whyCN: 「逐年」这个尺度标记把一般概念收窄为农人与水务管理者真正盯着的间隔。

senses.title: Slow swings over decades
senses.titleCN: 年代际的缓慢摆动
senses.definition: fluctuation with a period of ten to several tens of years, as in long ocean cycles
senses.definitionCN: 周期在十年至数十年之间的波动，如长周期的海洋振荡
senses.example: Decadal climate variability shifted the fish catch northward.
senses.exampleCN: 年代际气候变率把渔获推向北方。
senses.why: Because a slow swing looks like a trend within a short record, the decadal scale needs its own label inside the phrase.
senses.whyCN: 因为缓慢的摆动在短记录里看起来像趋势，年代际尺度需要在这个短语内部有自己的标记。

senses.title: Regional differences in the swing
senses.titleCN: 区域间波动的差异
senses.definition: differing amplitude or timing of fluctuation between regions under the same global mean
senses.definitionCN: 在同一全球均值下，各地区波动幅度或时间的不同
senses.example: Regional climate variability makes one valley flood while another dries.
senses.exampleCN: 区域气候变率使一个山谷发水，另一个却干裂。
senses.why: A global mean can hide opposite local swings, so the phrase is often qualified by region.
senses.whyCN: 全球均值会掩住局地相反的摆动，因此这个短语常以「区域」加以限定。

senses.title: The counterpart of forced change
senses.titleCN: 与强迫变化相对照的一面
senses.definition: the fluctuation treated as the background against which a forced trend must be detected
senses.definitionCN: 被当作背景的波动，被迫趋势必须从中被检出
senses.example: Detection studies must model climate variability before they can claim a trend.
senses.exampleCN: 检测研究必须先模拟气候变率，才能声称存在趋势。
senses.why: Statistics needs a noise model to find a signal, and the phrase supplies the noise side of that pair.
senses.whyCN: 统计需要噪声模型才能找到信号，这个短语提供这一对中的噪声面。

senses.title: Shifting frequency of extremes
senses.titleCN: 极端事件频率的起伏
senses.definition: the changing rate of droughts, floods or heat waves as the fluctuation changes
senses.definitionCN: 随着波动改变而变化的干旱、洪水或热浪频率
senses.example: Climate variability, not the trend alone, decides how often the levee is tested.
senses.exampleCN: 决定堤坝多久受一次考验的，是气候变率而非只有趋势。
senses.why: Impact studies care less about the mean than about how often the extremes arrive.
senses.whyCN: 影响研究关心的不是均值，而是极端事件到来的频次。

senses.title: Risk for farms and reservoirs
senses.titleCN: 农业与水利的风险
senses.definition: the practical uncertainty that fluctuation imposes on planning for water and crops
senses.definitionCN: 波动给水资源与作物规划带来的实际不确定性
senses.example: Irrigation schedules were built to absorb climate variability.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉日程的设计本就要吸纳气候变率。
senses.why: Planning converts a statistical property into a budget of risk, which is how the phrase is used in practice.
senses.whyCN: 规划把统计性质换算成一笔风险预算，这正是这个短语在实际中的用法。

intro.en: Climate variability joins Greek klima 'zone, slope' with Latin variare 'to vary'. Climate is a Greek loan; variability is a Latin-derived noun on the same stem as various. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climate variability 把希腊 klima「地带、斜面」与拉丁 variare「变化」组合起来。climate 是希腊借词；variability 是与 various 同词干的拉丁来源名词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Klima 'slope, inclination' named a belt of the earth defined by the sun's angle, and later the weather of such a belt.
items.cn: klima「斜面、倾斜」指按太阳角度划分的地带，后来指这种地带的天气。

items.en: Varius meant 'diverse, spotted, mottled'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes suggested to a root for 'change' is unproven.
items.cn: varius 意为「多样的、有斑点的、杂色的」。其更深来源不确定；有人把它与意为「变化」的词根联系，未获证实。

items.en: Variare 'to vary, change' came from varius, and gave English vary, various, variable and variation.
items.cn: variare「变化、改变」出自 varius，衍生英语 vary、various、variable 与 variation。

items.en: Variability was formed in English on variable with -ity, naming the quality of being changeable rather than a single change.
items.cn: variability 在英语中由 variable 加 -ity 构成，指「可变」这一性质，而非某一次变化。

items.en: In the twentieth century climate variability became the standard term for fluctuation that is not itself a trend.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，climate variability 成为指「本身并非趋势的波动」的标准术语。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of varius is unsettled, and any Indo-European form proposed for it is a reconstruction. The compound's first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：varius 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，为其提出的任何印欧形式均属重构。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds phrases built on climate that are often mistaken for this one; group two holds terms for change and for the spread of values.
note.cn: 第一组是同样以 climate 构成、常被误认作本词的短语；第二组是表示变化与数值离散的概念。

entries.definition: A lasting shift in the mean itself; variability is the wobble around a mean that need not move.
entries.definitionCN: 均值本身的持久移动；变率是围绕均值的抖动，均值未必移动。

entries.definition: A numerical simulation used to separate variability from forced change; it is an instrument, not a property.
entries.definitionCN: 用来把变率与强迫变化分开的数值模拟；它是工具，而非性质。

entries.definition: The warming expected from a doubling of carbon dioxide; it is a response to forcing, not internal wobble.
entries.definitionCN: 二氧化碳加倍时预期的升温；它是对强迫的响应，而非内部抖动。

entries.definition: Day-to-day fluctuation of weather; climate variability is the same idea averaged over seasons and years.
entries.definitionCN: 逐日天气的起伏；气候变率是把同一概念在季节与年尺度上平均。

entries.definition: Any rising and falling around a level; climate variability specifies the level as a climate statistic.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕某一水平的任何升降；气候变率把该水平限定为气候统计量。

entries.definition: A difference between cases or a single change; variability is the capacity or degree of such differences.
entries.definitionCN: 个案间的差异或某一次变化；variability 指这种差异的能力或程度。

entries.definition: A statistical measure of spread around a mean; it is the quantity that variability is often measured by.
entries.definitionCN: 衡量围绕均值离散程度的统计量；变率常用它来测量。

entries.definition: In detection studies, the part of a record not explained by forcing; it is variability seen as interference.
entries.definitionCN: 在检测研究中，记录里无法用强迫解释的部分；即被视为干扰的变率。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Varius meant mottled: variability is the mottling of a climate's numbers around their mean.
normal.cn: varius 意为杂色的：variability 就是气候数字围绕均值的斑驳。

normal.en: The family runs vary, various, variable, variation, variance and varied.
normal.cn: 同族词有 vary、various、variable、variation、variance 与 varied。

normal.en: Scale markers do the work: year-to-year, decadal and regional climate variability.
normal.cn: 尺度标记承担区别作用：年际、年代际与区域气候变率。

normal.en: The pair to remember is natural climate variability against human-forced change.
normal.cn: 要记住的对照是自然气候变率与人为强迫的变化。

normal.en: Extremes arrive through variability, which is why impact studies watch it.
normal.cn: 极端事件通过变率到来，因此影响研究盯着它。

abstract.en: Picture a road that wanders but never actually leaves the valley.
abstract.cn: 想象一条弯来弯去的路，却始终没有离开山谷。

abstract.en: Picture a tide going in and out while the harbour itself slowly sinks.
abstract.cn: 想象潮水涨落，而港口本身在慢慢下沉。

abstract.en: Picture a singer who holds one note but keeps breathing in and out.
abstract.cn: 想象一位歌手保持同一个音，却不断吸气呼气。

examples.en: Models must reproduce observed climate variability before their projections are trusted.
examples.cn: 模式必须先重现观测到的气候变率，其预估才可信。

examples.en: Natural climate variability can mask warming for a decade at a time.
examples.cn: 自然气候变率能一次把变暖遮掩十年。

examples.en: The study separated climate variability from the response to rising carbon dioxide.
examples.cn: 该研究把气候变率与对二氧化碳上升的响应分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「climate（气候）+ variability（变化性）」——气候的数字上下起伏 → 气候变率

root: 英语复合词：climate 来自希腊 klima「地带、斜面」（出自 klinein「倾斜」）；variability 来自拉丁 variare「变化」，出自 varius「杂色的、多样的」，varius 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one wobble: climate numbers mottle around a mean, the system generates it, it appears at yearly and decadal scales, it differs by region, it is the noise against which trends are detected, it changes how often extremes arrive, and it becomes a planning risk.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一种抖动展开：气候数字围绕均值斑驳起伏，系统自身产生它，它在年际与年代际尺度显现，随地区不同，是检出趋势时的噪声，改变极端事件到来的频次，最后成为规划中的风险。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wavy line rising and falling beside a nearly flat trend line.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条上下起伏的曲线，旁边是一条近乎平直的趋势线。

branches.en: DEFINITION: fluctuation around a mean is the whole content of the term.
branches.cn: 定义：围绕均值的波动就是这个术语的全部内容。

branches.en: NOISE SIDE: what the system makes on its own is what trends must be detected against.
branches.cn: 噪声面：系统自己造出的部分，正是检出趋势时必须对照的背景。

branches.en: TWO SCALES: yearly swings and decades-long swings look different in a record.
branches.cn: 两个尺度：年际摆动与数十年摆动在记录里样子不同。

branches.en: LOCAL AND EXTREME: the same global mean hides opposite regional swings and different rates of extremes.
branches.cn: 局地与极端：同一全球均值掩住相反的区域摆动与不同的极端频率。

branches.en: PLANNING RISK: statistics become a budget that farms and reservoirs must absorb.
branches.cn: 规划风险：统计变成农人与水库必须吸纳的预算。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek loan and a Latin-derived noun; the second element carries the productive family.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊借词与拉丁来源名词组合起来，派生词族主要在第二个成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin varius gives vary, various, variable, variation, variance and variability; Greek klima gives climate, climatic and acclimatize.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 varius 衍生 vary、various、variable、variation、variance 与 variability；希腊 klima 衍生 climate、climatic 与 acclimatize。

items.example: The belt had a dry klima.

items.exampleCN: 气候数据跨越一个世纪。

items.example: The cloth was varius in colour.
The variance doubled after the drought.
Variability is a quality, not an event.
items.exampleCN: 变率是一种性质，而非一次事件。

definition_zh: 气候模式；气候模型；对气候系统的数值模拟
definition_en: a mathematical simulation of the climate system used to study its behaviour and to project future conditions
core_image: 整个大气被切成一层层格子，每个格子里的温度与风都被写成数字在机器里运转
scene: 超级计算机房的屏幕上，一层层网格覆盖整个地球，每一格都在算自己的温度。A climate model turned the whole atmosphere into a grid of numbers.
sceneCN: 这里指「用方程与网格模拟气候系统的数值工具」（第 1 个义项：把气候系统写成方程并在计算机上求解的模拟）；句意为一个气候模式把整个大气变成了一张数字网格。图中可辨识物件：机柜、地球网格、屏幕曲线、温度色块。

senses.title: A numerical simulation of the climate system
senses.titleCN: 气候系统的数值模拟
senses.definition: a computer program that solves equations for the atmosphere, ocean, ice and land to simulate climate
senses.definitionCN: 求解大气、海洋、冰与陆地的方程以模拟气候的计算机程序
senses.example: A climate model turned the whole atmosphere into a grid of numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 一个气候模式把整个大气变成了一张数字网格。
senses.why: Model is Latin modulus, 'a small measure', from modus 'measure'; the word names a scaled-down version of a system, which is what the equations provide.
senses.whyCN: model 是拉丁 modulus「小尺度」，出自 modus「尺度」；这个词指系统按比例缩小的版本，而方程提供的正是这个版本。

senses.title: A global circulation model
senses.titleCN: 全球环流模式
senses.definition: a model that covers the whole planet and resolves large-scale circulation of atmosphere and ocean
senses.definitionCN: 覆盖整个行星并解析大气与海洋大尺度环流的模式
senses.example: The global climate model ran a century in a single afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 这个全球气候模式在一个下午里算完了一个世纪。
senses.why: Global fixes the domain, and circulation names the motion that the equations chiefly carry, so the compound specifies a class of model.
senses.whyCN: 「全球」限定范围，「环流」指明方程主要承载的运动，因此这个复合词指定了一类模式。

senses.title: A regional model nested inside a global one
senses.titleCN: 嵌套在全球模式中的区域模式
senses.definition: a high-resolution model run over a limited area, taking its boundaries from a global model
senses.definitionCN: 在有限区域上运行、边界条件取自全球模式的高分辨率模式
senses.example: The regional climate model resolved the valley winds the global one missed.
senses.exampleCN: 区域气候模式解析出全球模式漏掉的山谷风。
senses.why: Resolution costs computing, so modellers spend it where detail matters and call the result regional.
senses.whyCN: 分辨率消耗算力，因此建模者把算力花在需要细节的地方，并称其结果为区域模式。

senses.title: A simple energy-balance model
senses.titleCN: 简单的能量平衡模式
senses.definition: a stripped-down model that tracks only incoming and outgoing radiation for the whole planet
senses.definitionCN: 只追踪整个行星入射与出射辐射的简化模式
senses.example: An energy-balance climate model explains the first order in three equations.
senses.exampleCN: 一个能量平衡气候模式用三个方程就解释了一阶现象。
senses.why: The word model covers toys as well as supercomputer runs, since what matters is that a system is represented, not how finely.
senses.whyCN: model 既指玩具模型也指超算运行，要紧的是系统被表示出来，而不在于精细到何种程度。

senses.title: One member of an ensemble
senses.titleCN: 集合模拟中的一个成员
senses.definition: a single run within a group of runs that differ slightly in starting conditions or parameters
senses.definitionCN: 在一组起始条件或参数略有差异的运行中的一次运行
senses.example: Each climate model in the ensemble gave a slightly different decade.
senses.exampleCN: 集合中的每个气候模式都给出了略有不同的十年。
senses.why: Forecasting practice surrounds one model with many similar ones, and each of them is still called a model.
senses.whyCN: 预报实践用许多相似的模式围绕一个模式，其中每一个仍被称作 model。

senses.title: The tool behind scenario projections
senses.titleCN: 情景预估所依靠的工具
senses.definition: the model as the device that converts a scenario of emissions into a range of future climates
senses.definitionCN: 把一套排放情景换算成一组未来气候的装置
senses.example: The climate model translated the high-emission path into four degrees of warming.
senses.exampleCN: 气候模式把高排放路径换算成四度升温。
senses.why: Once a scenario is fed in, the model becomes the place where policy assumptions turn into temperatures.
senses.whyCN: 情景一旦输入，模式就成了政策假设变成温度的地方。

senses.title: A source of structured uncertainty
senses.titleCN: 结构性不确定性的来源
senses.definition: the model considered as a source of spread, since different structures produce different answers
senses.definitionCN: 被视为离散来源的模式，因为不同结构给出不同答案
senses.example: The spread between models is itself a result worth reporting.
senses.exampleCN: 模式之间的离散本身就是值得报告的结果。
senses.why: Because each model simplifies differently, disagreement between them is evidence about what is not known.
senses.whyCN: 因为每个模式的简化方式不同，模式间的不一致便成了关于未知之事的证据。

senses.title: Any simplified working picture
senses.titleCN: 比喻：对复杂局势的简化推演
senses.definition: a simplified scheme used to reason about a complicated situation
senses.definitionCN: 用来推演复杂局面的简化方案
senses.example: Her climate model of the market had three variables and no weather.
senses.exampleCN: 她对市场的「气候模式」只有三个变量，也没有天气。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the essential move: a complex system is replaced by a handful of equations you can turn.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了关键动作：复杂系统被换成几个可以拨动的方程。

intro.en: Climate model joins Greek klima 'zone' with Latin modulus 'small measure', from modus 'measure'. Both parts are old loans; the compound is twentieth-century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: climate model 把希腊 klima「地带」与拉丁 modulus「小尺度」组合起来，后者出自 modus「尺度」。两半都是古老的借词，复合词则是二十世纪的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Klima named a slope or a belt of the earth fixed by the sun's angle, and then the weather of that belt.
items.cn: klima 指斜面，或按太阳角度划定的地球地带，后指该地带的天气。

items.en: Modus meant 'measure, manner'. Its deeper origin is uncertain; the link sometimes proposed to a root for 'measure' is a reconstruction rather than a proven source.
items.cn: modus 意为「尺度、方式」。其更深来源不确定；有人提出的与「测量」词根的联系只是重构，并非已证实的来源。

items.en: Modulus, a diminutive of modus, meant 'a small measure' and was used for a standard or a scale model; English model comes from it through Italian and French.
items.cn: modulus 是 modus 的指小形式，意为「小尺度」，用于标准或按比例的模型；英语 model 经意大利语与法语来自它。

items.en: Model entered English meaning a pattern or an example, and only later a simplified representation of a system.
items.cn: model 进入英语时指范型或范例，后来才指系统的简化表示。

items.en: Twentieth-century numerical forecasting produced the first computer models of the atmosphere, and climate versions followed once runs could span decades.
items.cn: 二十世纪的数值预报造出最早的大气计算机模式，当运算能跨越数十年之后，气候版本随之出现。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Latin origin of modus is unsettled, so any Indo-European form cited for it is a reconstruction. The compound's first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：modus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，为其引用的任何印欧形式均属重构。复合词首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds climate terms that sound like tools but name other things; group two holds the modelling vocabulary that surrounds the phrase.
note.cn: 第一组是听起来像工具、实则指别的事物的气候术语；第二组是围绕这个短语的建模词汇。

entries.definition: A model run for days ahead from observed initial conditions; a climate model runs decades from boundary conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 由实测初始条件起算、预报数天的模式；气候模式则由边界条件起算数十年。

entries.definition: The numbers a model produces; the model is the tool, the output is what comes out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 模式算出的数字；模式是工具，输出是从中出来的东西。

entries.definition: The practice of building and running such models; the model is one artefact, modelling is the work.
entries.definitionCN: 构建与运行这类模式的实践；前者是一件成品，后者是这项工作。

entries.definition: The warming a model gives for doubled carbon dioxide; it is a number read off the model, not the model.
entries.definitionCN: 模式在二氧化碳加倍时给出的升温；它是从模式读出的一个数，而非模式本身。

entries.definition: Running a simplified system to see how it behaves; a climate model is one kind of simulation.
entries.definitionCN: 运行简化系统以观察其行为；气候模式是模拟的一种。

entries.definition: A consistent story of future emissions fed into a model; the scenario is input, the model is the engine.
entries.definitionCN: 输入模式的未来排放的连贯叙事；情景是输入，模式是引擎。

entries.definition: A future climate computed under stated assumptions; it comes from a model but is not the model.
entries.definitionCN: 在明确假设下算出的未来气候；它来自模式，但并非模式。

entries.definition: An organised explanation of why things happen; a model is a calculating representation that may encode a theory.
entries.definitionCN: 对事物为何发生的系统解释；模式是可能编码了理论的计算表示。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Modulus was a small measure: a model is the climate reduced to something you can measure and turn.
normal.cn: modulus 是小尺度：模式就是把气候缩成可以计算、可以拨动的东西。

normal.en: The family runs model, modelling, modeller, module, modular and modulate.
normal.cn: 同族词有 model、modelling、modeller、module、modular 与 modulate。

normal.en: Scale words separate the kinds: global climate model, regional climate model, energy-balance model.
normal.cn: 尺度词区分种类：全球气候模式、区域气候模式、能量平衡模式。

normal.en: Input is a scenario, output is a projection, and the spread between runs is an ensemble.
normal.cn: 输入是情景，输出是预估，多次运行间的离散是集合。

normal.en: Resolution is the price: finer grid, more computing.
normal.cn: 分辨率就是代价：网格越细，算力越多。

abstract.en: Picture a toy globe whose oceans are rows of numbers.
abstract.cn: 想象一个玩具地球，海洋是一行行数字。

abstract.en: Picture a board game that lets you replay a century in an afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一局棋，让你一个下午重演一个世纪。

abstract.en: Picture a weather map redrawn as a spreadsheet.
abstract.cn: 想象一张天气图被改画成一张表格。

examples.en: The climate model reproduces the observed cooling after large volcanic eruptions.
examples.cn: 这个气候模式重现了大型火山喷发后的观测降温。

examples.en: Downscaling a global climate model gives the region its own rainfall projection.
examples.cn: 对全球气候模式做降尺度，可为该地区给出自己的降水预估。

examples.en: Each climate model in the comparison used a different cloud scheme.
examples.cn: 参与比较的每个气候模式都用了不同的云方案。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「climate（气候）+ model（模型）」——把气候装进可计算的模型里 → 气候模式

root: 英语复合词：climate 来自希腊 klima「地带、斜面」；model 来自拉丁 modulus「小尺度」，出自 modus「尺度」，modus 更深来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one scaled-down machine: it simulates the system, it covers the globe or a region, it can be stripped to radiation only, it is one member of an ensemble, it turns scenarios into temperatures, it generates spread, and finally any complicated situation can be reduced to such a working picture.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一台缩小的机器展开：它模拟系统，覆盖全球或一个区域，也可只留下辐射，是集合中的一员，把情景换成温度，产生离散，最后任何复杂局面都能被缩成这样的工作图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the atmosphere cut into a grid, each cell holding a number that the machine advances.
core.cn: 核心意象：大气被切成网格，每格装一个数字，由机器向前推进。

branches.en: REPRESENTATION: whether full or stripped down, the point is a system turned into equations.
branches.cn: 表示：无论完整还是精简，要点都是把系统变成方程。

branches.en: DOMAIN: the same method covers the globe or one valley.
branches.cn: 范围：同一方法可覆盖全球，也可覆盖一条山谷。

branches.en: ENSEMBLE: one model is usually read beside its near-twins.
branches.cn: 集合：一个模式通常与它的近亲一起读。

branches.en: FROM STORY TO NUMBER: a scenario goes in, a temperature comes out, and disagreement becomes evidence.
branches.cn: 从故事到数字：情景输入，温度输出，不一致成为证据。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED PICTURE: any messy situation can be reduced to a few turnable variables.
branches.cn: 图景转移：任何纷乱局面都能被缩成几个可拨动的变量。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Greek loan with a Latin-derived noun whose root, modus, also builds mode, moderate and modify.
intro.cn: 这个短语把希腊借词与拉丁来源名词组合起来，其词根 modus 还构成 mode、moderate 与 modify。

latinIntro.en: Latin modus gives mode, moderate, modest, modify and modulus; Greek klima gives climate and climatic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 modus 衍生 mode、moderate、modest、modify 与 modulus；希腊 klima 衍生 climate 与 climatic。

items.example: The klima of the coast is mild.

items.meaning: a separate part of a system
items.exampleCN: 每个模块处理一个过程。

definition_zh: 海洋学；海洋研究；对海洋的系统考察
definition_en: the scientific study of the ocean, including its water, chemistry, life, geology and circulation
core_image: 一根钢缆从船尾垂进黑色的海面，仪器一路下沉，把深海的数字送回甲板
scene: 科考船在夜里放下采水器，钢缆一路往深处去，船舱的屏幕亮起一条条曲线。She dated her love of oceanography to a single cast of the wire.
sceneCN: 这里指「研究海洋的学科」（第 1 个义项：对海水、化学、生物、地质与环流的系统科学研究）；句意为她把对海洋学的热爱追溯到那一次放缆。图中可辨识物件：船尾、钢缆、采水器、屏幕曲线。

senses.title: The science of the sea as a whole
senses.titleCN: 把海洋作为整体研究的学科
senses.definition: the scientific study of the ocean as a physical, chemical, biological and geological system
senses.definitionCN: 把海洋作为物理、化学、生物与地质系统进行研究的科学
senses.example: She dated her love of oceanography to a single cast of the wire.
senses.exampleCN: 她把对海洋学的热爱追溯到那一次放缆。
senses.why: Ocean is Greek okeanos, the river thought to encircle the world; -graphy is Greek graphein 'to write'. The name therefore says 'writing down the ocean'.
senses.whyCN: ocean 是希腊 okeanos，古人想象中环绕世界的大河；-graphy 是希腊 graphein「书写」。因此这个名字说的是「把海洋写下来」。

senses.title: Physical oceanography
senses.titleCN: 物理海洋学
senses.definition: the branch that studies currents, waves, mixing, heat and salt transport
senses.definitionCN: 研究海流、波浪、混合、热量与盐分输运的分支
senses.example: Physical oceanography explains why the deep water forms near the poles.
senses.exampleCN: 物理海洋学解释了深层水为何在两极附近形成。
senses.why: Physics claimed the largest branch first, because navigation and climate both needed water movement quantified.
senses.whyCN: 物理学最先占据最大的分支，因为航海与气候都需要把海水运动量化。

senses.title: Chemical oceanography
senses.titleCN: 化学海洋学
senses.definition: the branch that studies dissolved substances, gases and the chemistry of seawater
senses.definitionCN: 研究溶解物质、气体与海水化学的分支
senses.example: Chemical oceanography traced the carbon stored in the deep Pacific.
senses.exampleCN: 化学海洋学追踪了储存在太平洋深处的碳。
senses.why: Seawater is a solution, so a whole branch reads the sea as a chemical system.
senses.whyCN: 海水是一种溶液，因此有一整个分支把海当作化学系统来读。

senses.title: Biological oceanography
senses.titleCN: 生物海洋学
senses.definition: the branch that studies marine life and its relation to the water around it
senses.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物及其与周围水体关系的分支
senses.example: Biological oceanography links the spring bloom to the light and nutrients above the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 生物海洋学把春季藻华与陆架之上的光与营养联系起来。
senses.why: Life in the sea depends on the water's chemistry and light, so the biological branch works inside the physical one.
senses.whyCN: 海中的生命依赖水的化学与光，因此生物分支在物理分支内部工作。

senses.title: Geological oceanography
senses.titleCN: 地质海洋学
senses.definition: the branch that studies the sea floor, sediments and the history recorded in them
senses.definitionCN: 研究海底、沉积物及其中所记历史的分支
senses.example: Geological oceanography read the ridge's growth from the magnetic stripes.
senses.exampleCN: 地质海洋学从磁条带读出洋脊的生长。
senses.why: The floor is an archive, and the geological branch treats the ocean as a place where earth history is written.
senses.whyCN: 海底是一份档案，地质分支把海洋当作书写地球历史的地方。

senses.title: The work of surveying at sea
senses.titleCN: 海上观测与调查的工作
senses.definition: the practice of going to sea to measure, sample and map
senses.definitionCN: 出海测量、采样与制图的实践活动
senses.example: Oceanography in that decade meant six weeks at sea each year.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个年代，海洋学意味着每年六周的海上作业。
senses.why: The -graphy in the name still carries its literal sense: the discipline is also the writing down that happens on deck.
senses.whyCN: 名字里的 -graphy 仍保留字面义：这门学科也包括在甲板上进行的记录。

senses.title: Applied oceanography
senses.titleCN: 应用海洋学
senses.definition: the use of ocean knowledge for navigation, fisheries, offshore industry and defence
senses.definitionCN: 把海洋知识用于航海、渔业、海上工业与防务
senses.example: Applied oceanography set the route that avoided the worst swell.
senses.exampleCN: 应用海洋学定出了避开最恶劣涌浪的航线。
senses.why: Practical demand funded much of the field, and its problems took the name of the science with an added adjective.
senses.whyCN: 实际需求资助了这门学科的许多部分，其问题便以这门科学之名加上一个形容词来称呼。

senses.title: A systematic sounding of any vast field
senses.titleCN: 比喻：对任何浩瀚领域的系统探究
senses.definition: a systematic, patient study of something vast and hard to see into
senses.definitionCN: 对某一浩瀚而难以看清之物的系统而耐心的研究
senses.example: Her oceanography of the archive took ten years and produced three maps.
senses.exampleCN: 她对档案的「海洋学」花了十年，绘出三张地图。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the two features of the science: the field is enormous, and knowledge comes only by lowering instruments into it.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留了这门科学的两个特征：领域极广，而知识只能靠把仪器放进去才得到。

intro.en: Oceanography joins Greek okeanos, the ocean, with -graphia 'writing, description'. The word was coined in the nineteenth century on Greek models. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oceanography 把希腊 okeanos「海洋」与 -graphia「书写、描述」组合起来。这个词是十九世纪依希腊语范式造出的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos in Homer is the river that encircles the world. Its own origin is uncertain; it may be a pre-Greek word, and no Indo-European etymology is agreed.
items.cn: 在荷马史诗中，okeanos 是环绕世界的大河。它自身的来源不确定，可能是前希腊语的词，尚无公认的印欧词源。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw, scratch'. It gives -graphy, graphic, grammar and diagram, all through the idea of marks made by hand.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、描画、刻划」。它衍生 -graphy、graphic、grammar 与 diagram，都围绕「用手留下的痕迹」这一意象。

items.en: Oceanography was formed in the nineteenth century to name the systematic description of the sea, alongside geography and cartography.
items.cn: oceanography 在十九世纪成形，用来命名对海洋的系统描述，与 geography、cartography 同属一类构词。

items.en: As expeditions multiplied, the word shifted from describing the sea to studying it with instruments.
items.cn: 随着考察次数增多，这个词从「描述海洋」转为「用仪器研究海洋」。

items.en: The twentieth century split the field into physical, chemical, biological and geological oceanography, each with its own methods.
items.cn: 二十世纪把这门学科分为物理、化学、生物与地质海洋学，各有自己的方法。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): the pre-Greek origin of okeanos is unsettled, so any form offered for it is a guess rather than a derivation. The first date of the English word is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：okeanos 在希腊语之前的来源无定论，为其提出的形式都是猜测而非派生。这个英语词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds look-alike names for related fields or for the same word's relatives; group two holds the wider or narrower names for studying the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是相邻学科或同一词族、外形相近的名称；第二组是研究海洋在范围上更宽或更窄的名称。

entries.definition: A synonym built on -logia 'study' rather than -graphia 'writing'; it is rarer and chiefly European.
entries.definitionCN: 以 -logia「研究」而非 -graphia「书写」构成的同义词，更少见，主要在欧洲使用。

entries.definition: The adjective describing what belongs to the field; the noun names the field itself.
entries.definitionCN: 描述属于该领域的形容词；名词则指领域本身。

entries.definition: A practitioner of the science; the discipline and its worker differ in suffix.
entries.definitionCN: 从事这门科学的人；学科与其从业者只在后缀上不同。

entries.definition: The measuring and charting of waters for navigation, a practical craft rather than the science as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 为航海测量并制图水域的实务技艺，而非整门科学。

entries.definition: An umbrella name for sea research in any combination of disciplines; oceanography is its classic core.
entries.definitionCN: 跨学科海洋研究的统称；海洋学是其中经典的核心。

entries.definition: The study of lakes and rivers; it shares methods with oceanography but not the salt water.
entries.definitionCN: 对湖泊与河流的研究；方法与海洋学相通，但对象不是咸水。

entries.definition: The study of sea life only; oceanography also covers water, chemistry, geology and circulation.
entries.definitionCN: 只研究海洋生命；海洋学还涵盖水体、化学、地质与环流。

entries.definition: The study of the atmosphere; air and sea are studied apart though they exchange heat and momentum.
entries.definitionCN: 对大气的研究；海与气虽交换热量与动量，却分科研究。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Okeanos was the world-circling river, and graphein is to write: oceanography is the writing down of that river.
normal.cn: okeanos 是环绕世界的大河，graphein 是书写：海洋学就是把那条河写下来。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographic, oceanographer and oceanarium.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographic、oceanographer 与 oceanarium。

normal.en: Four branches: physical, chemical, biological and geological oceanography.
normal.cn: 四个分支：物理、化学、生物与地质海洋学。

normal.en: Practical phrases: a degree in oceanography, study oceanography, applied oceanography.
normal.cn: 实用搭配：海洋学学位、研究海洋学、应用海洋学。

normal.en: The -graphy ending marks a descriptive science, as in geography and cartography.
normal.cn: -graphy 结尾标志一门描述性科学，如 geography 与 cartography。

abstract.en: Picture a wire lowered into the dark and a single number coming back.
abstract.cn: 想象一根钢缆垂进黑暗，回来时带来一个数字。

abstract.en: Picture a library whose shelves are all underwater and never fully read.
abstract.cn: 想象一座书架全在水下的图书馆，从未被读完。

abstract.en: Picture someone mapping a country by dropping plumb lines.
abstract.cn: 想象有人靠垂线测深来绘制一个国家的地图。

examples.en: Oceanography grew quickly once ships could carry reliable instruments.
examples.cn: 一旦船只能够携带可靠的仪器，海洋学便迅速发展。

examples.en: The department offers oceanography alongside meteorology.
examples.cn: 该系与气象学并设海洋学。

examples.en: Her oceanography of the deep basin filled a gap in the charts.
examples.cn: 她对深盆地的海洋学研究填补了海图上的空白。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ocean（海洋）+ graphy（书写）」——把海洋一笔一笔写下来 → 海洋学

root: 希腊语复合：okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（更深来源存疑）+ -graphia「书写、描述」，出自 graphein「书写」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one act of lowering instruments into a vast medium: the whole science, its four branches, the work at sea, its practical uses, and finally any patient sounding of something too large to see at once.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把仪器放进一片浩瀚介质之中——整门学科、它的四个分支、海上作业、实际应用，最后指对任何大到无法一眼看清之物的耐心探测。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wire lowered into black water, returning numbers to a lit deck.
core.cn: 核心意象：钢缆垂进黑水，把数字送回亮着灯的甲板。

branches.en: THE WHOLE: the name covers the sea as one system.
branches.cn: 整体：这个名字把海当作一个系统来覆盖。

branches.en: FOUR BRANCHES: water, chemistry, life and floor each get a share of the discipline.
branches.cn: 四个分支：水体、化学、生命与海底各分得这门学科的一份。

branches.en: WORK AT SEA: the writing in -graphy happens on deck, not only in libraries.
branches.cn: 海上作业：-graphy 里的「书写」发生在甲板上，而不只在图书馆。

branches.en: APPLIED USE: routes, fisheries and offshore work consume the knowledge.
branches.cn: 应用：航线、渔业与海上作业消耗这些知识。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED METHOD: any vast field can be sounded with patience.
branches.cn: 方法转移：任何浩瀚领域都能以耐心探测。

intro.en: Oceanography is a Greek-based compound, so its morphemes come from Greek rather than Latin and no Latin cognate family is offered.
intro.cn: oceanography 是以希腊语为基础的复合词，其语素来自希腊语而非拉丁语，因此不列拉丁同族词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin source here: okeanos and graphein are Greek, and the later Latin-speaking world borrowed the finished Greek compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁来源：okeanos 与 graphein 都是希腊语，后来的拉丁语世界只是借用了这些造好的希腊复合词。

items.example: The okeanos surrounded the known lands.
items.exampleCN: 这条大洋环绕已知的陆地。

items.example: The ocean carried the warm water north.
Oceanic plates sink at the trench.
items.exampleCN: 大洋板块在海沟处下沉。

items.example: The scribe wrote on the wax.

items.meaning: the writing down of the sea

items.exampleCN: 水道测量使航道保持标示。

definition_zh: 海洋学的；海洋考察的；海洋水文与地质的
definition_en: relating to the scientific study of the ocean or to the instruments and surveys used in it
core_image: 一排仪器挂在同一根钢缆上，温度、盐度、深度同时被记进同一条曲线
scene: 船尾的绞车把一串仪器放进海里，仪器一边下沉一边记录温度与盐度。The oceanographic survey mapped a deep ridge that no chart had shown.
sceneCN: 这里指「与海洋科学考察有关的」（第 1 个义项：属于海洋学或用于海洋研究的）；句意为这次海洋学调查测绘出一条海图上从未标出的深海脊。图中可辨识物件：绞车、仪器串、海面、测绘屏。

senses.title: Belonging to the science of the sea
senses.titleCN: 属于海洋科学的
senses.definition: relating to oceanography as a scientific discipline
senses.definitionCN: 与作为一门科学的海洋学有关的
senses.example: The oceanographic survey mapped a deep ridge that no chart had shown.
senses.exampleCN: 这次海洋学调查测绘出一条海图上从未标出的深海脊。
senses.why: Oceanographic is oceanography plus -ic, the Greek suffix for 'relating to', so it marks whatever belongs to the discipline.
senses.whyCN: oceanographic 是 oceanography 加 -ic（希腊语中表「与……有关」的后缀），因此标记属于这门学科的事物。

senses.title: Of the instruments and ships used
senses.titleCN: 属于海洋观测仪器与船只的
senses.definition: describing the equipment, vessels or techniques used to study the sea
senses.definitionCN: 描述研究海洋所用的设备、船只或技术
senses.example: The oceanographic winch paid out cable at two metres a second.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋考察绞车以每秒两米的速度放缆。
senses.why: An adjective naturally attaches to the tools of a trade, so the word covers hardware as well as theory.
senses.whyCN: 形容词自然可以附着于行业的工具，因此这个词既涵盖理论也涵盖硬件。

senses.title: Of water properties measured at sea
senses.titleCN: 属于海上测得的水文特征
senses.definition: relating to measured properties such as temperature, salinity, density and oxygen
senses.definitionCN: 与温度、盐度、密度、溶解氧等被测性质有关
senses.example: Oceanographic conditions favoured a strong autumn bloom.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋水文条件有利于秋季藻华。
senses.why: The science's basic output is a profile of properties with depth, and the adjective names those properties as a group.
senses.whyCN: 这门科学的基本产出是性质随深度的剖面，形容词便把这些性质作为一组来称呼。

senses.title: Of the sea floor and its sediments
senses.titleCN: 属于海底与沉积物的
senses.definition: relating to the geology of the ocean floor and the record held in its sediments
senses.definitionCN: 与海底地质及沉积物所载记录有关
senses.example: The oceanographic chart showed a fan of sediment beyond the shelf.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋地质图上显示出陆架之外的一片沉积扇。
senses.why: The geological branch works through the same adjective, since the sea floor is studied with the same expeditions.
senses.whyCN: 地质分支也使用同一个形容词，因为海底是在同一些航次中被研究的。

senses.title: Of biological sampling at sea
senses.titleCN: 属于海上生物采样的
senses.definition: relating to the sampling and counting of marine organisms during a survey
senses.definitionCN: 与调查期间对海洋生物的采样与计数有关
senses.example: Oceanographic nets brought up larvae from three hundred metres.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋生物网从三百米深处拖上幼体。
senses.why: Biology at sea borrows the adjective because it shares the ship, the wire and the station grid.
senses.whyCN: 海上生物学借用这个形容词，因为它共用同一艘船、同一根钢缆与同一套站位网格。

senses.title: Of a research cruise
senses.titleCN: 属于科考航次的
senses.definition: relating to an organised expedition that collects data at a series of stations
senses.definitionCN: 与在一系列站位采集数据的组织化航次有关
senses.example: The oceanographic cruise lasted forty days and never touched port.
senses.exampleCN: 这次海洋科考航次持续四十天，从未靠港。
senses.why: Cruises are the unit of field work, so the adjective often modifies the voyage rather than the science.
senses.whyCN: 航次是野外工作的单位，因此这个形容词常修饰航程而非学科。

senses.title: Of satellite observation of the sea
senses.titleCN: 属于卫星海洋遥感的
senses.definition: relating to remote sensing of sea surface temperature, colour, height and winds
senses.definitionCN: 与海表温度、水色、海面高度与风的遥感有关
senses.example: Oceanographic satellites see the surface, not the depth.
senses.exampleCN: 海洋遥感卫星看到的是表层，而非深处。
senses.why: Remote sensing widened the adjective's reach from ships to orbit while keeping the same object of study.
senses.whyCN: 遥感把这个形容词的适用范围从船只扩展到轨道，研究对象仍是同一个。

senses.title: Any large systematic survey
senses.titleCN: 比喻：任何大规模的系统调查
senses.definition: describing a wide, methodical investigation of something hard to reach
senses.definitionCN: 形容对难以触及之物的广泛而有条理的调查
senses.example: An oceanographic reading of the files found three forgotten contracts.
senses.exampleCN: 对这些档案的一次「海洋学式」通读，找出了三份被遗忘的合同。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the method rather than the water: many stations, one wire, patient coverage.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留的是方法而非海水：许多站点、一根钢缆、耐心的覆盖。

intro.en: Oceanographic is oceanography plus -ic, from Greek -ikos 'relating to'. The whole family is built on Greek okeanos and graphein. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oceanographic 是 oceanography 加 -ic，后者出自希腊 -ikos「与……有关」。整个词族建立在希腊 okeanos 与 graphein 上。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos named the river around the world. Its origin is uncertain and may be pre-Greek.
items.cn: okeanos 指环绕世界的大河。其来源不确定，可能是前希腊语。

items.en: Graphein 'to write, scratch' gives -graphia, and the compound oceanography names the description of the sea.
items.cn: graphein「书写、刻划」衍生 -graphia，复合词 oceanography 指对海洋的描述。

items.en: -Ikos formed adjectives meaning 'relating to'; Latin took it as -icus, and English now uses -ic.
items.cn: -ikos 构成意为「与……有关」的形容词；拉丁语取为 -icus，英语今用 -ic。

items.en: Oceanographic appears soon after oceanography, as expeditions began to produce charts, profiles and reports.
items.cn: oceanographic 紧接 oceanography 出现，当时考察开始产出图件、剖面与报告。

items.en: The adjective extended to instruments, cruises and satellites as the field industrialised.
items.cn: 随着这门学科工业化，这个形容词扩展到仪器、航次与卫星。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): okeanos has no agreed Indo-European origin, so any form proposed for it is a guess. The adjective's first date is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：okeanos 没有公认的印欧来源，为其提出的形式都是猜测。这个形容词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds near-identical forms of the same family; group two holds adjectives for sea, water and fieldwork that are easily substituted.
note.cn: 第一组是同一词族中外形几乎相同的形式；第二组是容易被替换的、表示海、水与野外作业的形容词。

entries.definition: The discipline itself; the adjective describes what belongs to it.
entries.definitionCN: 学科本身；形容词则描述属于它的事物。

entries.definition: A practitioner; the adjective cannot stand for a person.
entries.definitionCN: 从业者；形容词不能指人。

entries.definition: Relating to the ocean as a body of water, not to the science that studies it.
entries.definitionCN: 与作为水体的海洋有关，而非与研究它的科学有关。

entries.definition: An older, longer adjective built with -ical; it means the same as oceanographic.
entries.definitionCN: 以 -ical 构成的较旧较长的形容词，意义与 oceanographic 相同。

entries.definition: A general adjective for things of the sea, from Latin mare; it does not imply a research discipline.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指与海有关，来自拉丁 mare；不含研究学科之意。

entries.definition: Relating to navigation and seamanship rather than to scientific measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 与航海与船艺有关，而非科学测量。

entries.definition: Relating to the measurement and charting of navigable water, a practical rather than a research aim.
entries.definitionCN: 与可航水域的测量制图有关，目的偏实用而非研究。

entries.definition: Relating to the study of inland waters; it looks similar in method but names a different medium.
entries.definitionCN: 与研究内陆水体有关；方法相似，所指介质不同。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -ic is the Greek 'relating to': oceanographic means 'belonging to the writing down of the sea'.
normal.cn: -ic 是希腊语「与……有关」：oceanographic 意为「属于把海洋写下来这件事的」。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographer and oceanographic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographer 与 oceanographic。

normal.en: It modifies hardware as often as theory: oceanographic vessel, instrument, winch, data.
normal.cn: 它修饰硬件的频率不亚于理论：海洋科考船、仪器、绞车、数据。

normal.en: Four branches all use the adjective: physical, chemical, biological and geological.
normal.cn: 四个分支都用这个形容词：物理、化学、生物与地质。

normal.en: Satellites made the adjective orbital as well as seaborne.
normal.cn: 卫星使这个形容词既能指海上，也能指轨道。

abstract.en: Picture one wire carrying many instruments at once.
abstract.cn: 想象一根钢缆同时挂着许多仪器。

abstract.en: Picture a survey that visits a hundred points and draws one map.
abstract.cn: 想象一次调查走访上百个点，只画出一张图。

abstract.en: Picture someone reading a dark room with a single lamp on a long pole.
abstract.cn: 想象有人用长杆上的灯来读一间暗室。

examples.en: Oceanographic data from the mooring filled a decade-long gap.
examples.cn: 锚系设备提供的海洋学数据填补了长达十年的空白。

examples.en: The oceanographic vessel carried two winches and a coring rig.
examples.cn: 这艘海洋科考船配有两台绞车和一套取芯装置。

examples.en: Oceanographic conditions in the strait change with the tide.
examples.cn: 海峡的海洋水文条件随潮汐变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ocean（海洋）+ graphic（描绘的）」——把海洋描绘下来的 → 海洋学的

root: 希腊语来源：okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（更深来源存疑）+ graphein「书写」+ -ikos「与……有关的」；无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one adjective: it marks the discipline, its instruments, its measured water properties, its sea floor, its biological sampling, its cruises, its satellites and finally any wide systematic survey.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个形容词展开：它标记这门学科、其仪器、所测的水文性质、海底、生物采样、科考航次、卫星观测，最后指任何大规模系统调查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one wire carrying many instruments, all writing into the same profile.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根钢缆挂着许多仪器，全都写进同一条剖面。

branches.en: THE FIELD: the suffix -ic simply attaches the noun to whatever belongs to it.
branches.cn: 学科：后缀 -ic 把名词附着于属于它的一切。

branches.en: HARDWARE AND VOYAGE: ships, winches and cruises carry the adjective as readily as papers do.
branches.cn: 硬件与航程：船只、绞车与航次像论文一样自然带这个形容词。

branches.en: THREE OBJECTS: water properties, the floor and the organisms are all read on the same stations.
branches.cn: 三个对象：水文性质、海底与生物都在同一批站位上被读取。

branches.en: ORBIT: remote sensing stretches the adjective upward without changing its object.
branches.cn: 轨道：遥感把这个形容词向上延伸，对象未变。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED METHOD: many stations, one wire, patient coverage.
branches.cn: 方法转移：许多站点、一根钢缆、耐心的覆盖。

intro.en: Oceanographic is a Greek-derived adjective; the suffix is Greek and the stem is the Greek compound for sea description, so no Latin entries are given.
intro.cn: oceanographic 是希腊来源的形容词，后缀属希腊语，词干是希腊语中「描述海洋」的复合词，因此不列拉丁词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin borrowed the finished Greek forms but contributed no root here; ocean and -graphy are Greek all the way down.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语借用了造好的希腊形式，但在此没有贡献词根；ocean 与 -graphy 一路都是希腊语。

items.example: They wrote the depths in the log.
items.exampleCN: 他们把深处的情况写进日志。

items.example: Cartography is the writing of maps.
A physical question is about nature.
items.exampleCN: 一个「物理的」问题关乎自然。
一次海洋科考航次离开港口。
这个海湾在海洋学上很不寻常。

definition_zh: 海洋学家；海洋研究者；海洋调查人员
definition_en: a scientist who studies the ocean, its water, life, floor and circulation
core_image: 一个人站在甲板上，手里拿着记录板，身后的钢缆正往深海里放
scene: 深夜的实验室里，一个人对着满屏的浮标轨迹标出一股暖流的路径。The oceanographer traced the warm current from a year of buoy data.
sceneCN: 这里指「以研究海洋为职业的科学家」（第 1 个义项：研究海水、生物、海底与环流的科学工作者）；句意为这位海洋学家凭一年的浮标数据追出了那股暖流的路径。图中可辨识物件：浮标轨迹屏、海图、记录本、暖流箭头。

senses.title: A scientist of the sea
senses.titleCN: 研究海洋的科学家
senses.definition: a scientist whose work is the study of the ocean as a physical, chemical, biological and geological system
senses.definitionCN: 以研究海洋的物理、化学、生物与地质系统为工作的科学家
senses.example: The oceanographer traced the warm current from a year of buoy data.
senses.exampleCN: 这位海洋学家凭一年的浮标数据追出了那股暖流的路径。
senses.why: Oceanographer is the Greek compound for sea description with -graphos 'one who writes', so the word means 'one who writes down the sea'.
senses.whyCN: oceanographer 是希腊语中「描述海洋」的复合词加上 -graphos「书写者」，因此这个词意为「把海洋写下来的人」。

senses.title: A physical oceanographer
senses.titleCN: 物理海洋学家
senses.definition: one who studies currents, waves, mixing and the transport of heat and salt
senses.definitionCN: 研究海流、波浪、混合与热盐输运的人
senses.example: The physical oceanographer modelled the overflow across the sill.
senses.exampleCN: 这位物理海洋学家模拟了越过海槛的溢流。
senses.why: Physics supplies the equations for motion, so its practitioners take the main name with a branch adjective.
senses.whyCN: 物理学提供运动的方程，其从业者便在主名之前加一个分支形容词。

senses.title: A chemical oceanographer
senses.titleCN: 化学海洋学家
senses.definition: one who studies dissolved gases, nutrients and the chemistry of seawater
senses.definitionCN: 研究溶解气体、营养盐与海水化学的人
senses.example: The chemical oceanographer measured the oxygen minimum layer.
senses.exampleCN: 这位化学海洋学家测了最小含氧层。
senses.why: Seawater is a solution, so a chemist can spend a career on what is dissolved in it.
senses.whyCN: 海水是一种溶液，化学家可以终身研究其中溶解的东西。

senses.title: A geological oceanographer
senses.titleCN: 地质海洋学家
senses.definition: one who studies the sea floor, its sediments and the history they record
senses.definitionCN: 研究海底、其沉积物及所记历史的人
senses.example: The geological oceanographer dated the ash layer in the core.
senses.exampleCN: 这位地质海洋学家测定了岩芯中火山灰层的年代。
senses.why: The floor preserves a sequence, so a geologist reads the sea as a stratified archive.
senses.whyCN: 海底保存着层序，因此地质学家把海当作分层的档案来读。

senses.title: A biological oceanographer
senses.titleCN: 生物海洋学家
senses.definition: one who studies marine organisms and their relation to the water they live in
senses.definitionCN: 研究海洋生物及其与所处水体关系的人
senses.example: The biological oceanographer counted the copepods from each tow.
senses.exampleCN: 这位生物海洋学家数了每一网拖上来的桡足类。
senses.why: Life in the sea cannot be separated from the water, so the biological worker keeps the oceanographic name.
senses.whyCN: 海中的生命无法与海水分开，因此生物工作者也保留海洋学的名号。

senses.title: A member of a research cruise
senses.titleCN: 科考航次中的观测者
senses.definition: a scientist who sails on a research vessel to collect data at stations
senses.definitionCN: 随科考船出海、在各站位采集数据的科学家
senses.example: The oceanographer stood watch from midnight until four.
senses.exampleCN: 这位海洋学家从午夜值班到四点。
senses.why: Fieldwork defines the job as much as theory, and the person on watch is still called by the same name.
senses.whyCN: 野外工作与理论一样界定这份职业，值班的人仍用同一个称呼。

senses.title: An early surveying officer
senses.titleCN: 早期的海洋调查人员
senses.definition: in older usage, an officer or naturalist employed to sound and describe the sea
senses.definitionCN: 旧时受雇测深并描述海洋的军官或博物学者
senses.example: The oceanographer of the old survey filled four volumes with soundings.
senses.exampleCN: 那次旧调查的海洋调查员用四卷书记满了测深数据。
senses.why: Before specialised degrees, the -graphos sense was literal: the work was to write down what the lead line found.
senses.whyCN: 在专门学位出现之前，-graphos 的字面义仍在：工作就是把测锤探到的东西写下来。

senses.title: Anyone who sounds a vast unknown
senses.titleCN: 比喻：探究深不可测领域的人
senses.definition: a person who patiently investigates something vast and hard to see into
senses.definitionCN: 耐心探究某浩瀚而难以看清之物的人
senses.example: The oceanographer of the ministry's files knew where every report had sunk.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部委档案的「海洋学家」知道每份报告沉在哪里。
senses.why: The metaphor keeps the person and the method: someone who lowers a line into a place others cannot see.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻保留人与方法：一个人把测线垂进他人看不见的地方。

intro.en: Oceanographer joins Greek okeanos 'ocean' with -graphos 'one who writes', the personal form of graphein. The word is a nineteenth-century coinage. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: oceanographer 把希腊 okeanos「海洋」与 -graphos「书写者」组合起来，后者是 graphein 的人称形式。这个词是十九世纪的造词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Okeanos was the river encircling the world. Its origin is uncertain and probably pre-Greek.
items.cn: okeanos 是环绕世界的大河。其来源不确定，可能属前希腊语。

items.en: Graphein meant 'to write, draw, scratch', and its agent noun -graphos named a person who writes or draws.
items.cn: graphein 意为「书写、描画、刻划」，其施动名词 -graphos 指书写或描画的人。

items.en: Okeanos plus -graphos gave a word for one who describes the sea, built on the same pattern as geographer and cartographer.
items.cn: okeanos 加 -graphos 构成指「描述海洋的人」的词，与 geographer、cartographer 依同一范式。

items.en: As systematic expeditions began, the word moved from the writer of descriptions to the salaried scientific officer on a survey ship.
items.cn: 随着系统考察开始，这个词从「写描述的人」转为调查船上领薪的科学职员。

items.en: In the twentieth century the oceanographer became a trained specialist with a degree, a branch and a set of instruments.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，oceanographer 成了一位受过训练、有学位、有分支与一套仪器的专家。

items.en: Source uncertain (root only): okeanos has no accepted Indo-European origin, so any form offered for it is a guess. The first date of the English word is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅词根）：okeanos 没有公认的印欧来源，为其提出的任何形式都是猜测。这个英语词的首见年代只能约计。

note.en: Group one holds the family forms of the same word; group two holds names for people who work on or with the sea.
note.cn: 第一组是同一个词族中的各种形式；第二组是从事海洋工作或在海上工作者的名称。

entries.definition: The field of study; the -grapher form names the person who practises it.
entries.definitionCN: 研究领域；-grapher 形式指从事它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to the field or its work; it cannot name a person.
entries.definitionCN: 与领域或其工作有关；不能指人。

entries.definition: One who describes the earth's surface, built with the same -graphos; different object, same pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 描述地表的人，用同一个 -graphos 构成；对象不同，范式相同。

entries.definition: One who writes with light; the -graphos element survives with a very different medium.
entries.definitionCN: 以光书写的人；-graphos 这一成分在完全不同的媒介中留存。

entries.definition: A specialist in sea life; an oceanographer may study water, floor or circulation instead.
entries.definitionCN: 研究海洋生命的专家；海洋学家也可能研究水体、海底或环流。

entries.definition: One who measures and charts waters for navigation, a practical calling rather than a research career.
entries.definitionCN: 为航海测量并制图水域的人，属实务行业而非研究职业。

entries.definition: A scientist of the atmosphere; the two fields meet where sea and air exchange heat.
entries.definitionCN: 研究大气的科学家；两门学科在海气交换热量处相接。

entries.definition: A scientist of lakes and rivers, using similar tools on a different body of water.
entries.definitionCN: 研究湖泊与河流的科学家，用相似工具研究不同的水体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: -graphos is 'one who writes': an oceanographer is the person who writes down the sea.
normal.cn: -graphos 是「书写者」：oceanographer 就是把海洋写下来的人。

normal.en: The family runs ocean, oceanic, oceanography, oceanographic and oceanographer.
normal.cn: 同族词有 ocean、oceanic、oceanography、oceanographic 与 oceanographer。

normal.en: Branch adjectives name the speciality: physical, chemical, biological and geological oceanographer.
normal.cn: 分支形容词点出专长：物理、化学、生物与地质海洋学家。

normal.en: The pattern matches geographer and cartographer, both -grapher words.
normal.cn: 这个范式与 geographer、cartographer 相同，都是 -grapher 词。

normal.en: Watchkeeping is part of the job: the oceanographer stands a four-hour shift at sea.
normal.cn: 值班是工作的一部分：海洋学家在海上值四小时的班。

abstract.en: Picture someone holding a notebook on a deck while a wire disappears below.
abstract.cn: 想象有人站在甲板上拿着本子，钢缆在下方消失。

abstract.en: Picture a reader who keeps a lamp on a long pole to see the dark shelves.
abstract.cn: 想象一位读者用长杆上的灯去照黑暗的书架。

abstract.en: Picture a person who maps a country one sounding at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人一次一个测深点地绘出一个国家。

examples.en: The oceanographer spent three seasons on the same seamount.
examples.cn: 这位海洋学家在同一座海山上度过了三个季节。

examples.en: A chemical oceanographer joined the cruise to sample dissolved iron.
examples.cn: 一位化学海洋学家加入航次，采集溶解铁样品。

examples.en: The oceanographer's chart became the standard reference for the strait.
examples.cn: 这位海洋学家的海图成了该海峡的标准参考。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ocean（海洋）+ grapher（书写者）」——把海洋写下来的人 → 海洋学家

root: 希腊语来源：okeanos「环绕世界的大河」（更深来源存疑）+ -graphos「书写者」，出自 graphein「书写」；无拉丁同族，拉丁词条留空。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one person: the scientist of the sea, four branch specialists, the watchkeeper on a cruise, the early surveying officer, and finally anyone who lowers a line into a place others cannot see.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个人展开：研究海洋的科学家，四位分支专家，航次上的值班者，早期的调查官员，最后指任何把测线垂进他人看不见之处的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person on deck with a notebook while the wire goes down.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人拿着本子站在甲板上，钢缆正向深处去。

branches.en: THE ROLE: -graphos fixes the person, and ocean fixes the object.
branches.cn: 角色：-graphos 定人，ocean 定对象。

branches.en: FOUR SPECIALITIES: water, chemistry, floor and life each produce a branch expert.
branches.cn: 四种专长：水体、化学、海底与生命各自产生一位分支专家。

branches.en: THE WATCH: the job is also a shift on deck, not only a degree.
branches.cn: 值班：这份职业也是甲板上的一班岗，而不只是一纸学位。

branches.en: EARLIER FORM: before degrees, the writing was literal and the title belonged to survey officers.
branches.cn: 较早形态：在学位之前，书写是字面的，名号属于调查官员。

branches.en: TRANSFERRED PERSON: anyone patient enough to sound a dark place inherits the figure.
branches.cn: 人物转移：任何有耐心探测黑暗之处的人都继承了这一形象。

intro.en: Oceanographer is a Greek-derived personal noun; the suffix -graphos is Greek, so no Latin entries are listed.
intro.cn: oceanographer 是希腊来源的人称名词，后缀 -graphos 属希腊语，因此不列拉丁词条。

latinIntro.en: No Latin root is involved: okeanos and graphein are Greek, and the -graphos suffix reached English through Latin and French borrowings of Greek compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 这里不涉及拉丁词根：okeanos 与 graphein 是希腊语，-graphos 后缀是经拉丁语与法语借用希腊复合词而进入英语的。

items.example: They wrote the soundings each hour.
items.exampleCN: 他们每小时记录一次测深。
一位「大地书写者」描述了海岸。

items.meaning: a person who writes or records
one who writes down the sea
items.exampleCN: 海洋学家记了航海日志。
海洋学需要长时间的航次。
传记作者读了每一封信。
